A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. These three instruments are identified together as the Parliamentary Accountability Triangle, ensuring cabinet responsibility to the legislature.

mcqs.question: What is the maximum number of questions listed for oral answer per day as Starred Questions?
mcqs.explanation: A maximum of 20 questions may be listed for oral answer per day as Starred Questions.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: A Starred Question requires an oral answer on the floor of the House.
Statement B: Supplementary questions are allowed on a Starred Question.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: A Starred Question receives an oral answer on the floor of the House, and supplementary questions are permitted.

mcqs.question: An Unstarred Question requires which type of answer?
options: A short-notice answer without a written record
An oral answer on the floor of the House
A written answer laid on the table
An answer only through an Adjournment Motion
mcqs.explanation: An Unstarred Question requires a written answer laid on the table.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding an Unstarred Question is incorrect?
options: The answer is laid on the table.
It permits supplementary questions on the floor of the House.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that supplementary questions are permitted. Supplementary questions are not allowed for an Unstarred Question.

mcqs.question: A Short Notice Question relates to:
options: A matter that can be raised only after a full debate
A matter of urgent public importance
A matter requiring a written answer only
A matter concerning only parliamentary privileges
mcqs.explanation: A Short Notice Question relates to a matter of urgent public importance.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A Short Notice Question receives an oral answer and permits supplementary questions.
Reason (R): It is asked with shorter notice than the standard prescribed period.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the shorter notice explains the timing of the question, not why an oral answer and supplementary questions are permitted.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Question Hour
(b) Zero Hour
(c) Question Hour
(d) Zero Hour

List-II
(i) Indian parliamentary innovation
(ii) Formal procedure under Parliamentary Rules
(iii) Questioning Ministers on administrative actions
(iv) Raising urgent matters of public importance without prior notice
mcqs.explanation: Question Hour is a formal procedure under Parliamentary Rules and questions Ministers on administrative actions. Zero Hour is an Indian parliamentary innovation for raising urgent matters of public importance without prior notice.

mcqs.question: Zero Hour originated as an Indian parliamentary innovation in the:
mcqs.explanation: Zero Hour originated as an Indian parliamentary innovation in the early 1960s.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about Zero Hour is incorrect?
options: It immediately follows Question Hour in Lok Sabha.
It is formally codified in Parliamentary Rules.
Its duration is not fixed as a matter of formal rules.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that Zero Hour is formally codified in Parliamentary Rules. It is an informal convention and its duration is not fixed.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Question Hour has a maximum duration of one hour.
Statement B: Zero Hour in Lok Sabha generally lasts up to one hour.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Question Hour has a maximum duration of one hour, while Zero Hour in Lok Sabha generally lasts up to one hour.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Calling Attention Motion
(b) Adjournment Motion
(c) Calling Attention Motion
(d) Adjournment Motion

List-II
(i) Traditional parliamentary device
(ii) Indian parliamentary innovation
(iii) Does not disrupt the scheduled daily agenda
(iv) Interrupts and suspends normal parliamentary business
mcqs.explanation: Calling Attention Motion is an Indian parliamentary innovation and does not disrupt the scheduled daily agenda. Adjournment Motion is a traditional parliamentary device that interrupts and suspends normal business.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Calling Attention Motion has no condemnation or censure element.
Statement B: Adjournment Motion involves censure or condemnation of the Government.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Calling Attention Motion has no condemnation or censure element, whereas Adjournment Motion involves censure or condemnation of the Government.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding an Adjournment Motion:
I. It must relate to a single, definite and specific matter of recent occurrence.
II. It may raise a question of privilege.
III. Only one Adjournment Motion is allowed per sitting.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and III are correct. An Adjournment Motion must concern a single, definite, specific matter of recent occurrence, cannot raise a question of privilege, and only one is allowed per sitting.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are requirements or restrictions relating to an Adjournment Motion?

1. It must concern a single matter.
2. The matter must be definite and specific.
3. The matter must be of recent occurrence.
4. Only one Adjournment Motion is allowed per sitting.
mcqs.explanation: All four listed points are requirements or restrictions relating to an Adjournment Motion.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Zero Hour and Calling Attention Motion are indigenous Indian contributions to parliamentary procedure.
Reason (R): Both are identified as Indian parliamentary innovations.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Zero Hour and Calling Attention Motion are described as Indian parliamentary innovations and therefore as indigenous contributions to parliamentary procedure.

mcqs.question: The primary objective of a Calling Attention Motion is to:
options: Call the attention of a Minister to an urgent public matter
Condemn the Government for a definite matter
Obtain a written answer laid on the table
mcqs.explanation: The primary objective of a Calling Attention Motion is to call the attention of a Minister to an urgent public matter.

mcqs.question: What is the scheduled time for Question Hour in the Lok Sabha?
mcqs.explanation: In the Lok Sabha, Question Hour is held from 11:00 AM to 12:00 Noon.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following correctly describes the timing of Question Hour in the Rajya Sabha after 2014?
mcqs.explanation: Question Hour in the Rajya Sabha is held from 12:00 Noon to 1:00 PM, having been shifted after 2014.

mcqs.question: Question Hour is devoted to which activity during the first hour of every parliamentary sitting?
mcqs.explanation: The first hour of every parliamentary sitting is dedicated to asking and answering questions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding Zero Hour is incorrect?
options: It is a formal procedure codified in the Parliamentary Rules.
It is an Indian parliamentary innovation.
It immediately follows Question Hour in the Lok Sabha.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that Zero Hour is formally codified in the Parliamentary Rules. It is an informal convention and its duration is not fixed.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Question Hour and Zero Hour have different procedural statuses.
Reason (R): Question Hour is formally codified in the Parliamentary Rules, whereas Zero Hour is an informal convention.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The formal codification of Question Hour and the informal status of Zero Hour explain their different procedural statuses.

mcqs.question: What is the maximum duration generally indicated for Zero Hour in the Lok Sabha?
options: It has a constitutionally fixed duration of three hours
mcqs.explanation: Zero Hour in the Lok Sabha generally lasts up to one hour, although its duration is not fixed in the Rules.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding an Adjournment Motion:
I. It must relate to a single, definite and specific matter of recent occurrence.
II. It cannot raise a question of privilege.
III. Only one Adjournment Motion is allowed per sitting.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct requirements or restrictions relating to an Adjournment Motion.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Calling Attention Motion — impact on scheduled business
(b) Adjournment Motion — impact on scheduled business
(c) Calling Attention Motion — censure element
(d) Adjournment Motion — censure element

List-II
(i) Involves censure or condemnation of the Government
(ii) Does not disrupt the scheduled daily agenda
(iii) No condemnation or censure element
(iv) Interrupts and suspends normal parliamentary business
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Calling Attention—does not disrupt the agenda (a-ii); Adjournment—interrupts and suspends business (b-iv); Calling Attention has no censure element (c-iii); Adjournment involves censure (d-i).

mcqs.question: Historically, the operational scope of which parliamentary motion was restricted by Calling Attention notices?
mcqs.explanation: Calling Attention notices historically restricted the operational scope of Adjournment Motions, not that of Question Hour or Zero Hour.

mcqs.question: An Adjournment Motion is admissible only when which condition is satisfied?
options: Other tools, such as a Short Duration discussion, are too late
The matter concerns a question of privilege
A matter has already been fully debated in Question Hour
The scheduled daily agenda has been completed
mcqs.explanation: An Adjournment Motion is admissible only when other tools, such as a Short Duration discussion, are too late to address the matter.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Zero Hour immediately follows Question Hour in the Lok Sabha.
Statement B: Zero Hour is used for raising urgent matters of public importance without prior notice.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Zero Hour follows Question Hour in the Lok Sabha and permits the raising of urgent matters of public importance without prior notice.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly states the timing of Zero Hour in the Lok Sabha?
options: Generally up to one hour, but without a specified time period
The first hour of every parliamentary sitting, irrespective of the House
mcqs.explanation: Zero Hour in the Lok Sabha runs from 12:00 Noon to 1:00 PM. It immediately follows Question Hour, which runs from 11:00 AM to 12:00 Noon in the Lok Sabha.

mcqs.question: What is the primary objective of an Adjournment Motion?
options: To raise urgent matters of public importance without prior notice as an informal convention
To discuss a definite matter of urgent public importance
To call the attention of a Minister to an urgent public matter
To question Ministers about administrative actions during the first hour
mcqs.explanation: The primary objective of an Adjournment Motion is to discuss a definite matter of urgent public importance. It interrupts and suspends normal parliamentary business.

mcqs.question: Parliamentary Questions are raised during which period of a parliamentary sitting?
mcqs.explanation: Parliamentary Questions are raised during Question Hour, which is the first hour of every parliamentary sitting.

mcqs.question: The primary purpose of Parliamentary Questions is to ensure:
mcqs.explanation: Parliamentary Questions are raised during Question Hour to ensure executive accountability.

mcqs.question: Parliamentary Questions are primarily addressed to whom?
mcqs.explanation: Parliamentary Questions are primarily addressed to Ministers to scrutinize administrative policies and government actions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not one of the three primary categories of Parliamentary Questions?
mcqs.explanation: The three primary categories are Starred, Unstarred and Short Notice Questions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding a Starred Question is incorrect?
options: It is marked with an asterisk.
There is no daily limit on such questions.
Supplementary questions may be asked after the oral answer.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the absence of a daily limit. A maximum of 20 questions per day are listed for oral answers.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A Starred Question permits supplementary questions.
Reason (R): A Starred Question receives an oral answer on the floor of the House.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Supplementary questions are permitted because the answer is given orally on the floor of the House.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Type of answer of a Starred Question
(b) Supplementary questions for an Unstarred Question
(c) Distinctive identification of a Short Notice Question
(d) Subject matter of a Short Notice Question

List-II
(i) No supplementary questions
(ii) Matter of urgent public importance
(iii) Oral answer
(iv) Shorter notice period
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Starred Question—oral answer; Unstarred Question—no supplementary questions; Short Notice Question—shorter notice period and urgent public importance.

mcqs.question: What type of answer is given to an Unstarred Question?
options: Written answer laid on the Table
Written answer followed by compulsory debate
Oral answer only in a committee
Oral answer on the floor of the House
mcqs.explanation: An Unstarred Question receives a written answer laid on the Table.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about an Unstarred Question is incorrect?
options: The answer is laid on the Table.
It is identified by an asterisk.
mcqs.explanation: The altered detail is the asterisk. An Unstarred Question has no asterisk mark.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Supplementary questions cannot be asked after an Unstarred Question.
Reason (R): An Unstarred Question receives a written answer laid on the Table.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Unstarred Question is answered in writing rather than orally, so supplementary questions are not permitted.

mcqs.question: A Short Notice Question must relate specifically to:
options: A matter of urgent public importance
A matter of ordinary public importance only
A matter concerning judicial appointments only
A matter concerning parliamentary privileges only
mcqs.explanation: A Short Notice Question must specifically concern a matter of urgent public importance.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding a Short Notice Question is incorrect?
options: It requires a standard prescribed notice period.
It concerns a matter of urgent public importance.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the notice period. A Short Notice Question is accepted with a shorter notice period than ordinary questions.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Supplementary questions can be asked after a Short Notice Question.
Reason (R): A Short Notice Question is answered orally.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Short Notice Question is answered orally, allowing supplementary questions.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Starred Questions and Short Notice Questions both permit supplementary questions.
Statement B: Unstarred Questions and Short Notice Questions both receive written answers.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true because both Starred and Short Notice Questions permit supplementary questions. Statement B is false because a Short Notice Question receives an oral answer.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Starred Questions are marked with an asterisk.
II. Unstarred Questions have no asterisk mark.
III. Short Notice Questions are identified by an asterisk.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. A Short Notice Question is distinguished by a shorter notice period, not by an asterisk.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Starred Question
(b) Unstarred Question
(c) Short Notice Question
(d) Starred Question

List-II
(i) Standard prescribed notice
(ii) Maximum 20 questions listed per day for oral answer
(iii) Shorter than standard notice
(iv) No strict 20-per-day limit
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Starred Question—maximum 20 oral questions per day and standard prescribed notice; Unstarred Question—no strict 20-per-day limit; Short Notice Question—shorter than standard notice.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. Starred Questions receive oral answers.
2. Unstarred Questions permit supplementary questions.
3. Short Notice Questions concern urgent public importance.
4. Starred Questions are marked with an asterisk.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because supplementary questions are not permitted for Unstarred Questions.

mcqs.question: What is the maximum number of questions listed per day for oral answer?
mcqs.explanation: The daily listing limit for oral answers is a maximum of 20 questions.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Starred Questions deal with general or ordinary public importance.
II. Unstarred Questions deal with matters of urgent public importance.
III. Short Notice Questions deal with matters of urgent public importance.
IV. Starred Questions have a standard prescribed notice period.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, III and IV are correct. Unstarred Questions, like Starred Questions, concern general or ordinary public importance, not specifically urgent public importance.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Starred Question
(b) Unstarred Question
(c) Short Notice Question
(d) Unstarred Question

List-II
(i) Oral answer and supplementary questions permitted
(ii) Written answer and no supplementary questions
(iii) Oral answer on the floor of the House
(iv) Standard prescribed notice
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Starred Question—oral answer with supplementary questions; Unstarred Question—written answer with no supplementary questions; Short Notice Question—oral answer; Unstarred Question—standard prescribed notice.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Starred Questions have a strict daily limit of 20 questions for oral answers.
Statement B: Unstarred Questions have no strict 20-per-day limit.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. A maximum of 20 Starred Questions are listed daily for oral answers, while Unstarred Questions have no strict 20-per-day limit.

mcqs.question: The daily listing of Short Notice Questions is at the discretion of whom?
options: The Leader of the House only
mcqs.explanation: The daily listing of Short Notice Questions is at the discretion of the Speaker or Chairman.

mcqs.question: Parliamentary Committees primarily serve as a mechanism of parliamentary control over administration by performing which function?
options: Handling detailed and complex legislative scrutiny
Framing the day-to-day agenda of the House only
Regulating the official parliamentary timetable only
mcqs.explanation: Parliamentary Committees act as a primary mechanism of parliamentary control over administration and handle detailed and complex legislative scrutiny.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Standing Committees are permanent and continuous in nature.
Reason (R): They are reconstituted annually or periodically.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Standing Committees are permanent and continuous, while annual or periodic reconstitution is a separate feature and does not explain their permanent nature.

mcqs.question: How many Department-Related Standing Committees are there, and how are they distributed between the two Houses?
options: 30: 20 under Lok Sabha and 10 under Rajya Sabha
22: 15 under Lok Sabha and 7 under Rajya Sabha
24: 8 under Lok Sabha and 16 under Rajya Sabha
24: 16 under Lok Sabha and 8 under Rajya Sabha
mcqs.explanation: There are 24 DRSCs: 16 under Lok Sabha and 8 under Rajya Sabha, with an approximately 2:1 joint ratio.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Public Accounts Committee
(b) Estimates Committee
(c) Committee on Public Undertakings
(d) Department-Related Standing Committees

List-II
(i) 24 committees
(ii) 30 members
(iii) 22 members
(iv) 22 members
mcqs.explanation: PAC has 22 members, the Estimates Committee has 30, COPU has 22, and there are 24 DRSCs.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Estimates Committee consists of 30 Lok Sabha members only.
The Committee on Public Undertakings has 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha members.
The Estimates Committee has 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha members.
The Public Accounts Committee has 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha members.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is the fourth. The Estimates Committee consists of 30 Lok Sabha members only and has no Rajya Sabha representation.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Public Accounts Committee examines CAG audit reports.
Reason (R): The Committee on Public Undertakings examines PSU-related CAG reports.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but COPU's examination of PSU-related CAG reports does not explain the PAC's examination of CAG audit reports.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Members of the three Financial Committees are elected through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
Statement B: Each of the three Financial Committees has a tenure of one year.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: PAC, the Estimates Committee and COPU use proportional representation by STV for election, and each has a one-year tenure.

mcqs.question: Which committee examines whether delegated executive rule-making remains within statutory limits?
mcqs.explanation: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation examines regulations, bye-laws and sub-rules to determine whether they remain within statutory limits.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Committee on Government Assurances
(b) Committee on Petitions
(c) Business Advisory Committee
(d) Rules Committee

List-II
(i) Recommends amendments to Rules of Procedure
(ii) Examines petitions and representations
(iii) Regulates the parliamentary timetable
(iv) Tracks assurances given by Ministers
mcqs.explanation: Government Assurances tracks ministerial assurances; Petitions examines petitions; Business Advisory regulates the timetable; Rules recommends procedural changes.

mcqs.question: When was the Lok Sabha Ethics Committee first constituted as an ad-hoc committee?
mcqs.explanation: The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee was first constituted as an ad-hoc committee on 16 May 2000.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee was made permanent in 2015.
Statement B: It can take up matters that are sub-judice.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The Ethics Committee was made permanent in 2015, but it cannot take up sub-judice matters.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Drafting Committee
(b) Union Constitution Committee
(c) Provincial Constitution Committee
(d) Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee

List-II
(i) J.B. Kripalani
(ii) Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
(iii) Jawaharlal Nehru
(iv) Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
mcqs.explanation: The Drafting Committee was chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar; the Union Constitution Committee by Jawaharlal Nehru; the Provincial Constitution Committee by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel; and the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee by J.B. Kripalani.

mcqs.question: Who chaired the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribals?
mcqs.explanation: The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribals was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Jawaharlal Nehru chaired both the Union Constitution Committee and the Union Powers Committee.
Reason (R): These committees dealt respectively with the Union constitutional structure and the federal legislative division.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The subjects of the two committees describe their focus but do not explain why Nehru chaired both.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. H.C. Mukherjee chaired the Minorities Sub-Committee.
II. Dr. Rajendra Prasad chaired the Rules of Procedure Committee.
III. K.M. Munshi chaired the Order of Business Committee.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct: H.C. Mukherjee chaired the Minorities Sub-Committee, Dr. Rajendra Prasad the Rules of Procedure Committee, and K.M. Munshi the Order of Business Committee.

mcqs.question: How many members did the Drafting Committee originally have?
mcqs.explanation: The Drafting Committee had a total of 7 members.

mcqs.question: On which date was the Ad-hoc Committee on the National Flag appointed?
mcqs.explanation: The Ad-hoc Committee on the National Flag was appointed on 23 June 1947.

mcqs.question: Who chaired the 2G Spectrum Joint Parliamentary Committee constituted in 2011?
mcqs.explanation: The 2G Spectrum JPC of 2011 was chaired by P.C. Chacko.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following committees bar Ministers from being elected or nominated as members?

1. Public Accounts Committee
2. Estimates Committee
3. Committee on Public Undertakings
4. Committee on Subordinate Legislation
5. Committee on Petitions
mcqs.explanation: All five listed committees bar Ministers from membership: the three Financial Committees, the Committee on Subordinate Legislation and the Committee on Petitions.

mcqs.question: What is the defining feature of an Ad-hoc Committee of Parliament?
options: It is constituted for a specific inquiry or task and ceases after submitting its report
It regulates the official timetable of House business
It examines petitions submitted to the House
It is permanent and reconstituted annually
mcqs.explanation: Ad-hoc Committees are temporary bodies constituted for a specific inquiry or task. They cease to exist after submitting their report.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee has been appointed from the Opposition since 1967.
Reason (R): The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Speaker appoints the Chairman, while selection of the Chairman from the Opposition since 1967 is a separate convention and is not explained by the appointment authority alone.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Committee on Subordinate Legislation
(b) Committee on Petitions
(c) Business Advisory Committee
(d) Order of Business Committee

List-II
(i) Day-to-day agenda framing
(ii) Regulation of House business timetable
(iii) Examination of petitions and representations
(iv) Examination of delegated rule-making within statutory limits
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Subordinate Legislation–delegated rule-making within statutory limits; Petitions–petitions and representations; Business Advisory–House timetable; Order of Business–day-to-day agenda.

mcqs.question: Who chaired the Order of Business Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
mcqs.explanation: K.M. Munshi chaired the Order of Business Committee, which dealt with day-to-day agenda framing.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Drafting Committee is incorrect?
options: B.L. Mitter and D.P. Khaitan were among its original members.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.
N. Madhava Rau and T.T. Krishnamachari were original members and were later replaced.
The Committee originally had seven members.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the direction of replacement. B.L. Mitter and D.P. Khaitan were replaced by N. Madhava Rau and T.T. Krishnamachari.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Ad-hoc Committees cease to exist after submitting their report.
Statement B: Consultative Committees are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. Ad-hoc Committees end after submitting their report, while Consultative Committees are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Chairman of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the Speaker from the ruling party.
II. The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker from the Opposition since 1967.
III. The Chairman of the Committee on Public Undertakings is appointed by the Speaker from the Opposition since 1967.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. The Estimates Committee Chairman is appointed from the ruling party, while the PAC Chairman has been appointed from the Opposition since 1967. The note does not assign that convention to the COPU Chairman.

mcqs.question: Which parliamentary committee is described as the single largest parliamentary committee, with 30 members?
mcqs.explanation: The Estimates Committee has 30 members and is identified as the single largest parliamentary committee.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the Committee on Petitions is incorrect?
options: The Lok Sabha Committee on Petitions has 15 members.
Ministers may be elected or nominated as members of the Committee on Petitions.
It examines petitions and representations submitted to the House.
The Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions has 10 members.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that Ministers may be members. Ministers are barred from membership of the Committee on Petitions.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Committee on Subordinate Legislation has 15 members in each House.
Reason (R): Ministers are barred from membership of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the bar on Ministers does not explain the Committee's strength of 15 members in each House.

mcqs.question: Which committee regulates the official parliamentary timetable and programme of House business?
mcqs.explanation: The Business Advisory Committee regulates the official parliamentary timetable and programme of House business.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Steering Committee
(b) Order of Business Committee
(c) Rules of Procedure Committee
(d) Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee

List-II
(i) Part III guarantees
(ii) Assembly procedural rules
(iii) Steering Assembly business
(iv) Day-to-day agenda framing
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Steering Committee–Assembly business; Order of Business–day-to-day agenda; Rules of Procedure–procedural rules; Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee–Part III guarantees.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following committees were chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad?

1. Rules of Procedure Committee
2. Steering Committee
3. Ad-hoc Committee on the National Flag
4. Order of Business Committee
mcqs.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad chaired the Rules of Procedure Committee, Steering Committee and Ad-hoc Committee on the National Flag. The Order of Business Committee was chaired by K.M. Munshi.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Union Constitution Committee dealt with the Union Powers and the central constitutional structure.
Statement B: The Union Powers Committee dealt with the federal legislative division.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Union Constitution Committee addressed the Union Powers and central constitutional structure, while the Union Powers Committee dealt with federal legislative division.

mcqs.question: How many members were included in the 2G Spectrum Joint Parliamentary Committee constituted in 2011?
mcqs.explanation: The 2G Spectrum Joint Parliamentary Committee constituted in 2011 had 30 members: 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The 2G Spectrum Joint Parliamentary Committee was an Ad-hoc Joint Committee.
Reason (R): It was constituted in 2011 with 20 Lok Sabha members and 10 Rajya Sabha members.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Its membership composition does not explain why it was an Ad-hoc Joint Committee; the two statements describe different features.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribals was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
II. The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee was chaired by J.B. Kripalani.
III. The Minorities Sub-Committee was chaired by H.C. Mukherjee.
IV. The Provincial Constitution Committee was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. The Provincial Constitution Committee was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, not Jawaharlal Nehru.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Drafting Committee
(b) Provincial Constitution Committee
(c) Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribals
(d) Minorities Sub-Committee

List-II
(i) H.C. Mukherjee
(ii) Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
(iii) Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
(iv) Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Drafting Committee–Dr. B.R. Ambedkar; Provincial Constitution Committee–Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel; Advisory Committee–Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel; Minorities Sub-Committee–H.C. Mukherjee.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements about parliamentary committees are correct?

1. Standing Committees are permanent and continuous in nature.
2. Ad-hoc Committees are temporary.
3. Ad-hoc Committees are constituted for a specific inquiry or task.
4. Consultative Committees are parliamentary committees per se.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect because Consultative Committees are not parliamentary committees per se.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Committee on Government Assurances
(b) Rules Committee
(c) Committee on Petitions
(d) Committee on Subordinate Legislation

List-II
(i) Examines petitions and representations submitted to the House
(ii) Examines whether delegated executive rule-making stays within statutory limits
(iii) Tracks promises and assurances given by Ministers on the floor of the House
(iv) Recommends amendments and procedural adjustments to the Rules of Procedure
mcqs.explanation: The Committee on Government Assurances tracks ministerial promises; the Rules Committee recommends changes to procedural rules; the Committee on Petitions examines petitions; and the Committee on Subordinate Legislation checks delegated rule-making against statutory limits.

mcqs.question: Who chaired the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
mcqs.explanation: The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee was chaired by J.B. Kripalani and dealt with the Part III guarantees.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Consultative Committees are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.
Statement B: Consultative Committees are parliamentary committees in the same sense as Standing Committees.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Consultative Committees are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, but they are not parliamentary committees per se.

mcqs.question: Which pair correctly identifies the members who replaced B.L. Mitter and D.P. Khaitan in the Drafting Committee?
options: N. Madhava Rau and T.T. Krishnamachari
Jawaharlal Nehru and Dr. Rajendra Prasad
K.M. Munshi and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
mcqs.explanation: The original Drafting Committee included B.L. Mitter and D.P. Khaitan; they were replaced by N. Madhava Rau and T.T. Krishnamachari.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Consultative Committees may include MPs from specific zones or ministries.
II. Consultative Committees are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.
III. Consultative Committees are classified as parliamentary committees per se.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. Consultative Committees include MPs from specific zones or ministries and are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs; they are not parliamentary committees per se.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Consultative Committees are distinct from parliamentary committees.
Reason (R): They are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Their constitution by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs explains why Consultative Committees are not parliamentary committees per se.

mcqs.question: What is the tenure of each of the three Financial Committees of Parliament?
options: The term of the Lok Sabha
mcqs.explanation: The Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings each have a tenure of one year.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Department-Related Standing Committees follow an approximate 2:1 distribution between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
Reason (R): There are 16 Department-Related Standing Committees under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The distribution of 16 DRSCs under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha produces the approximate 2:1 ratio.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Parliamentary Committees
(b) Financial Committees
(c) Department-Related Standing Committees
(d) Inquiry Committees

List-II
(i) Examples of Standing Committees dealing with departments
(ii) Examples of Ad-hoc Committees
(iii) Broadly classified into Standing and Ad-hoc Committees
(iv) Examples of Standing Committees

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
mcqs.explanation: Parliamentary Committees are broadly classified into Standing and Ad-hoc Committees. Financial Committees and Department-Related Standing Committees are examples of Standing Committees, while Inquiry Committees are examples of Ad-hoc Committees.

mcqs.question:
Match each committee with the function associated with it:

List-I
(a) Public Accounts Committee
(b) Estimates Committee — budget function
(c) Estimates Committee — administrative function
(d) Committee on Public Undertakings

List-II
(i) Scrutiny of appropriation accounts and wasteful expenditure
(ii) Examination of budget estimates
(iii) Suggestion of economy in administration and administrative efficiency
(iv) Scrutiny of public-sector undertaking accounts and commercial soundness

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
mcqs.explanation: The Public Accounts Committee scrutinizes appropriation accounts and wasteful expenditure. The Estimates Committee examines budget estimates and suggests economy and administrative efficiency, while the Committee on Public Undertakings examines PSU accounts and commercial soundness.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee oversees the moral conduct of members.
Statement B: The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee oversees the ethical conduct of members.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee oversees both the moral and ethical conduct of members.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Provincial Constitution Committee dealt with the provincial constitutional framework.
II. The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, and Tribals was the parent committee for rights and minorities.
III. The Minorities Sub-Committee dealt with minority safeguards.
IV. The Provincial Constitution Committee dealt with minority safeguards.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. The Provincial Constitution Committee dealt with the provincial constitutional framework, the Advisory Committee was the parent committee for rights and minorities, and the Minorities Sub-Committee dealt with minority safeguards; statement IV wrongly assigns the last function to the Provincial Constitution Committee.

mcqs.question: Under Article 324, which body conducts elections for the President, Vice-President, Parliament and State Legislatures?
mcqs.explanation: The Election Commission of India conducts elections for the President, Vice-President, Parliament and State Legislatures under Article 324.

mcqs.question: The State Election Commission conducts elections to which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: Under Articles 243K and 243ZA, the State Election Commission conducts elections for Panchayats and Municipalities.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Lok Sabha Speaker and Deputy Speaker are chosen internally by the Lok Sabha under Article 93.
The Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman is chosen internally under Article 89(2).
The Election Commission of India elects the Chairman of a State Legislative Council under Article 182.
The Assembly Speaker and Deputy Speaker are chosen internally by the Assembly under Article 178.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that the Election Commission elects the Council Chairman. The Council Chairman is chosen internally by the Legislative Council under Article 182.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Election notifications for Parliamentary elections are issued by the President.
Reason (R): The Election Commission recommends dates and administers the election schedule.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The President issues notifications for Parliamentary elections, while the Election Commission recommends dates and administers the schedule; the latter does not explain the President’s authority to issue the notification.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Election disputes are adjudicated exclusively by the Judiciary through election petitions.
Statement B: Disputes concerning Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections are handled exclusively by the Election Commission.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true. Statement B is false because Presidential and Vice-Presidential election disputes are handled exclusively by the Supreme Court under Article 71.

mcqs.question: The right to vote and the right to be elected are treated as which type of rights?
mcqs.explanation: The notes classify the right to vote and the right to be elected as legal or statutory rights, not Fundamental Rights.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding electoral arrangements:
List-I
(a) President
(b) Vice-President
(c) Lok Sabha
(d) Rajya Sabha

List-II
(i) Direct election by citizens; FPTP
(ii) Elected MLAs of respective States; PR + STV
(iii) Elected MPs and elected MLAs; PR + STV
(iv) All MPs, elected and nominated; PR + STV
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are President–elected MPs and MLAs, Vice-President–all MPs, Lok Sabha–direct FPTP election, and Rajya Sabha–elected MLAs with PR + STV.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the Presidential election:
I. Nominated MPs and nominated MLAs cannot vote.
II. Members of Legislative Councils cannot vote.
III. The nomination requires 50 proposers and 50 seconders.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The Presidential electoral college excludes nominated MPs/MLAs and MLCs, and the nomination requirement is 50 proposers and 50 seconders.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): State Legislatures have no role in the election of the Vice-President.
Reason (R): The Vice-President is elected by all MPs of both Houses, including nominated MPs.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the composition of the Vice-Presidential electoral college explains why State Legislatures have no role.

mcqs.question: Which electoral system is used for elections to the Lok Sabha?
options: Proportional Representation by Single Transferable Vote
mcqs.explanation: Lok Sabha members are directly elected by citizens through the First-Past-the-Post system.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the First-Past-the-Post system is incorrect?
options: The candidate with the highest vote count wins.
The winning candidate need not secure 50 per cent or more of the votes.
A candidate must secure more than 50 per cent of the votes to win.
The system is used for Lok Sabha elections.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the requirement of more than 50 per cent of votes. Under FPTP, the candidate with the highest vote count wins, even without an absolute majority.

mcqs.question:
Match the constitutional Articles with the corresponding presiding officers or House:
List-I
(a) Article 93
(b) Article 178
(c) Article 89(2)
(d) Article 182

List-II
(i) Legislative Council Chairman
(ii) Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman
(iii) Lok Sabha Speaker and Deputy Speaker
(iv) Legislative Assembly Speaker and Deputy Speaker
mcqs.explanation: Article 93 concerns the Lok Sabha Speaker and Deputy Speaker, Article 178 the Assembly Speaker and Deputy Speaker, Article 89(2) the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman, and Article 182 the Council Chairman.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the composition of a Legislative Council:
I. One-third of its members are elected by MLAs.
II. One-third are elected by Local Bodies.
III. One-twelfth are elected by Graduates.
IV. One-sixth are nominated by the Governor.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements correctly state the specified categories and proportions for the Legislative Council.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the Legislative Council is incorrect?
options: Industrialists constitute an electoral category for the Legislative Council.
The Legislative Council is elected through proportional representation by means of the Single Transferable Vote.
The minimum age mentioned for the Legislative Council is 30 years.
One-twelfth of its members are elected by Teachers.
mcqs.explanation: The altered detail is the inclusion of industrialists. Industrialists are not an electoral category for the Legislative Council.

mcqs.question: Members of a State Legislative Assembly are elected through which method?
options: Direct election by citizens of the State using FPTP
Indirect election by all MPs using FPTP
Direct election by Local Bodies using PR + STV
Indirect election by elected MLAs using PR + STV
mcqs.explanation: The Legislative Assembly is directly elected by citizens of the State through the First-Past-the-Post system.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. The minimum age mentioned for Legislative Council membership is 30 years.
2. The minimum age mentioned for Panchayat and Municipality membership is 21 years.
3. The voting age is 21 years.
4. Voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 years.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Ward members and Panchs are directly elected by local voters.
Statement B: Elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are conducted by the Election Commission of India.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Ward members and Panchs are directly elected by local voters. However, Panchayat and Municipality elections are conducted by the State Election Commission.

mcqs.question: Which additional areas are included in the Presidential electoral college through the 70th Constitutional Amendment Act?
options: Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
mcqs.explanation: The Presidential electoral college includes elected MLAs of Delhi and Puducherry through the 70th Constitutional Amendment Act.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A Presidential election cannot be challenged or delayed merely because vacancies exist in the electoral college.
Reason (R): Article 71(4) provides that such vacancies do not invalidate or postpone the election.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and Article 71(4) directly explains why vacancies in the electoral college cannot be used to challenge or delay a Presidential election.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The value of an MLA’s vote varies from State to State based on population ratios.
Statement B: The value of an MP’s vote is uniform across all MPs.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. MLA vote value varies among States according to population ratios, whereas the MP vote value is uniform across all MPs.

mcqs.question: The voting age in India was lowered from 21 to 18 years by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
mcqs.explanation: The voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 years through the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988, which became effective in 1989.

mcqs.question: For nomination in the Presidential election, a candidate must have how many proposers and seconders?
mcqs.explanation: The Presidential election requires 50 proposers and 50 seconders for a nomination.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The President is elected through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
Reason (R): The Presidential election is conducted by secret ballot.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Proportional representation by single transferable vote describes the electoral system, while secret ballot describes the voting method; the latter does not explain the former.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected by citizens registered in territorial electoral rolls.
Statement B: Elections to the Lok Sabha are conducted through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true. Lok Sabha elections use the First-Past-the-Post system, not proportional representation by single transferable vote, so Statement B is false.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Rajya Sabha is incorrect?
options: Seats are allocated equally among all the States.
Its members are elected by the elected MLAs of the respective States.
Seats are allocated on the basis of population.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that seats are allocated equally among all States. The notes state that Rajya Sabha allocation is based on population, not equal allocation.

mcqs.question: Who elects the elected members of the Rajya Sabha from a State?
options: Directly elected citizens of the State
Members of the State Legislative Council of the respective State
Members of the State Legislative Assembly of the respective State
mcqs.explanation: The elected MLAs of the respective States elect the members of the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Statement B: The Vice-President is a member of the Rajya Sabha.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha but is not a member of the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the electoral categories for a Legislative Council is incorrect?
options: One-third of the members are elected by MLAs.
One-third of the members are elected by Local Bodies.
One-twelfth of the members are elected by Teachers.
mcqs.explanation: Industrialists are not an electoral category for the Legislative Council. The listed categories include MLAs, Local Bodies, Graduates, Teachers and Governor-nominated members.

mcqs.question: What is the minimum age mentioned for membership in Panchayats and Municipalities?
mcqs.explanation: The minimum age mentioned for Panchayat and Municipality membership is 21 years.

mcqs.question: Article 326 is associated with which electoral principle?
mcqs.explanation: The notes associate Article 326 with Universal Adult Suffrage.

mcqs.question: Who issues the election notification for elections to a State Legislature?
mcqs.explanation: Election notifications for State Legislature elections are issued by the Governor. The Election Commission recommends dates and administers the schedule.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Nominated MLAs cannot vote in Rajya Sabha elections.
II. Members of Legislative Councils cannot vote in Rajya Sabha elections.
III. Rajya Sabha elections are conducted by direct election of citizens.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are true according to the listed restrictions. Statement III is false because Rajya Sabha elections are indirect and involve elected MLAs of the respective States.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following offices use proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote?
1. President
2. Vice-President
3. Lok Sabha
4. Rajya Sabha
mcqs.explanation: The President, Vice-President and Rajya Sabha use proportional representation by single transferable vote. The Lok Sabha uses the First-Past-the-Post system, so the number is three.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) President
(b) Vice-President
(c) Lok Sabha
(d) Rajya Sabha

List-II
(i) Direct election through territorial electoral rolls
(ii) Indirect election by all MPs
(iii) Indirect election by elected MLAs of respective States
(iv) Indirect election through the Presidential electoral college
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: President–indirect election through the Presidential electoral college; Vice-President–indirect election by all MPs; Lok Sabha–direct election through territorial electoral rolls; Rajya Sabha–indirect election by elected MLAs of respective States.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. One-sixth of the members of a Legislative Council are nominated by the Governor.
II. One-twelfth of the members are elected by Graduates.
III. One-twelfth of the members are elected by Teachers.
IV. Industrialists are included as a separate electoral category.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III correctly state the composition categories. Statement IV is false because industrialists are not an electoral category.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The President is elected under Article 54.
II. The Vice-President is elected under Article 66.
III. The Lok Sabha is constituted under Article 81.
IV. The Legislative Assembly is provided for under Article 170.
V. The Legislative Council is provided for under Article 171.
options: I, III, IV and V only
I, II, III, IV and V
mcqs.explanation: All five statements are correct. Articles 54, 66, 81, 170 and 171 respectively relate to the President, Vice-President, Lok Sabha, Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Elected Members of the Lok Sabha form part of the Presidential electoral college.
Statement B: Elected Members of the Rajya Sabha form part of the Presidential electoral college.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Presidential electoral college includes elected Members of both Houses of Parliament.

mcqs.question: The Vice-Presidential election uses which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: The Vice-Presidential election is conducted through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote using a secret ballot.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the voting method used in a Legislative Council election?
options: Direct election by citizens of the State
mcqs.explanation: The Legislative Council election uses a secret ballot. The other options refer to electoral arrangements associated with direct elections or the Legislative Assembly framework.

mcqs.question: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to organise Village Panchayats as units of self-government?
mcqs.explanation: Article 40, a Directive Principle of State Policy, directs the State to organise Village Panchayats as units of self-government.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Charles Metcalfe described Indian village communities as “Little Republics”.
The Government of India Act, 1919 made Local Self-Government a Reserved Subject under provincial dyarchy.
Madras was the first Municipal Corporation, established in 1688.
Lord Ripon is recognised as the Father of Local Self-Government in India.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is “Reserved Subject”. The Government of India Act, 1919 made Local Self-Government a Transferred Subject under provincial dyarchy.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Local Self-Government is an exercise in democratic decentralisation.
Reason (R): It promotes community participation and local accountability.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Democratic decentralisation is linked with community participation and local accountability.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Balwant Rai Mehta Committee
(b) Ashok Mehta Committee
(c) Hanumantha Rao Committee
(d) L.M. Singhvi Committee

List-II
(i) Constitutional status and greater financial resources
(ii) Two-tier model and separate Nyaya Panchayats
(iii) Three-tier Panchayati Raj
(iv) Decentralisation of powers and finance and district planning bodies
mcqs.explanation: Balwant Rai Mehta recommended the three-tier system; Ashok Mehta recommended a two-tier model and separate Nyaya Panchayats; Hanumantha Rao focused on decentralisation and district planning; L.M. Singhvi recommended constitutional status and greater financial resources.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the first Municipal Corporation at Madras
B. Lord Ripon’s Resolution on Local Self-Government
C. Local Self-Government becoming a Transferred Subject under the Government of India Act
D. Introduction of Panchayati Raj in Rajasthan
mcqs.explanation: The correct sequence is Madras Municipal Corporation in 1688, Lord Ripon’s Resolution in 1882, the Government of India Act in 1919, and Panchayati Raj in Rajasthan in 1959.

mcqs.question:
Match the amendment with its principal domain and enforcement date.

List-I
(a) 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act
(b) 74th Constitutional Amendment Act
(c) 73rd Amendment enforcement
(d) 74th Amendment enforcement

List-II
(i) Urban Local Self-Government
(ii) 24 April 1993
(iii) Rural Local Self-Government
(iv) 1 June 1993
mcqs.explanation: The 73rd Amendment concerns rural Panchayats and was enforced on 24 April 1993. The 74th concerns urban municipalities and was enforced on 1 June 1993.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX of the Constitution.
II. Part IX contains Articles 243 to 243-O.
III. The 74th Amendment inserted Part IX-A.
IV. Part IX-A contains Articles 243P to 243ZG.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Part IX concerns Panchayats, while Part IX-A concerns Municipalities.

mcqs.question:
Match the level or area with the corresponding institution.

List-I
(a) Village level
(b) Block level
(c) District level
(d) Transitional urban area

List-II
(i) Nagar Panchayat
(ii) Gram Panchayat
(iii) Zila Parishad
(iv) Panchayat Samiti
mcqs.explanation: The rural tiers are Gram Panchayat at village level, Panchayat Samiti at block level and Zila Parishad at district level. A transitional urban area has a Nagar Panchayat.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Gram Sabha is the village-level general assembly of all persons registered in the village electoral rolls.
Reason (R): The Gram Sabha is the elected executive body of the village.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: The Assertion is true under Article 243A. The Reason is false because the elected executive body is the Gram Panchayat, whereas the Gram Sabha comprises registered voters.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The fixed term of Panchayats and Municipalities is five years.
Statement B: If a local body is dissolved prematurely, elections must always be held within six months, even when the remaining term is less than six months.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true. Statement B is false because elections within six months are not required when the remaining term is less than six months.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are included among local-government functional areas?
1. Public health
2. Sanitation
3. Water supply
4. Judicial review
mcqs.explanation: Public health, sanitation and water supply are included local-government functions. Judicial review is not a local-government function.

mcqs.question: Under Article 243B, the intermediate tier of Panchayati Raj is optional for States with a population of:
mcqs.explanation: The intermediate tier, represented by the Panchayat Samiti, is optional for States with a population of 20 lakh or less.

mcqs.question:
Match the constitutional provision with its subject.

List-I
(a) Article 243D
(b) Article 243E
(c) Article 243G
(d) Article 243K

List-II
(i) Powers and responsibilities
(ii) Reservations
(iii) State Election Commission
(iv) Tenure and dissolution
mcqs.explanation: Article 243D concerns reservations, Article 243E tenure and dissolution, Article 243G powers and responsibilities, and Article 243K the State Election Commission.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the accounts and audit of Panchayats?
options: The audit arrangement is dealt with under Article 243J.
The State Legislature provides for maintenance of Panchayat accounts.
Panchayat audit laws are enacted by the Union Parliament.
The State Legislature provides for audit of Panchayat accounts.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is “Union Parliament”. Under Article 243J, the State Legislature provides for the maintenance and audit of Panchayat accounts.

mcqs.question: Which State introduced Panchayati Raj first in India?
mcqs.explanation: Rajasthan was the first Panchayati Raj State, with its first implementation at Nagaur District on 2 October 1959. Andhra Pradesh followed second.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed in 1957.
II. The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee is recognised as the Architect of Panchayati Raj.
III. The G.V.K. Rao Committee was concerned with revitalisation and the representative character of Panchayats.
IV. The L.M. Singhvi Committee was appointed in 1977–78.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. The L.M. Singhvi Committee was associated with 1986, while 1977–78 refers to the Ashok Mehta Committee.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The State Election Commission is responsible for the superintendence, direction and conduct of local elections.
Reason (R): The State Finance Commission is constituted every five years by the Governor to review local finance distribution.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the State Finance Commission’s function does not explain the State Election Commission’s electoral responsibility. These are separate provisions under Articles 243K/243ZA and 243-I/243-Y respectively.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Article 243A
(b) Article 243-I
(c) Article 243J
(d) Article 243ZD

List-II
(i) State Finance Commission
(ii) Gram Sabha
(iii) District Planning Committee
(iv) Accounts and audit
mcqs.explanation: Article 243A concerns the Gram Sabha; Article 243-I the State Finance Commission; Article 243J accounts and audit; and Article 243ZD the District Planning Committee.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. The 73rd Amendment relates to rural Local Self-Government.
2. The 74th Amendment relates to urban Local Self-Government.
3. The 73rd Amendment is associated with the 11th Schedule containing 29 functional subjects.
4. The 74th Amendment is associated with the 12th Schedule containing 18 functional subjects.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. The 73rd Amendment concerns Panchayats and the 11th Schedule, while the 74th concerns Municipalities and the 12th Schedule.

mcqs.question: Which committee recommended the revitalisation and representative character of Panchayats?
mcqs.explanation: The G.V.K. Rao Committee, constituted in 1985, recommended the revitalisation and representative character of Panchayats.

mcqs.question: Who described Indian village communities as “Little Republics”?
mcqs.explanation: Charles Metcalfe described Indian village communities as “Little Republics”.

mcqs.question: Who is recognized as the Father of Local Self-Government in India?
mcqs.explanation: Lord Ripon is recognized as the Father of Local Self-Government in India because of his 1882 Resolution.

mcqs.question: The first Panchayati Raj system was inaugurated in which district on 2 October 1959?
mcqs.explanation: The first Panchayati Raj system was started in Rajasthan’s Nagaur District on 2 October 1959.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) 11th Schedule
(b) 12th Schedule
(c) Part IX
(d) Part IX-A

List-II
(i) Urban Local Self-Government
(ii) Rural Local Self-Government
(iii) 29 Functional Subjects
(iv) 18 Functional Subjects
mcqs.explanation: The 11th Schedule contains 29 functional subjects and relates to rural local government; the 12th Schedule contains 18 and relates to urban local government. Part IX concerns rural local government, while Part IX-A concerns urban local government.

mcqs.question: Part IX-A of the Constitution relating to Municipalities comprises which range of Articles?
mcqs.explanation: Part IX-A, dealing with Municipalities, comprises Articles 243P to 243ZG.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The District Planning Committee is referred to in Article 243ZD.
Statement B: The Metropolitan Planning Committee is referred to in Article 243ZE.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The notes identify the District Planning Committee with Article 243ZD and the Metropolitan Planning Committee with Article 243ZE.

mcqs.question: Under Article 243C, who regulates the composition of Panchayats and Municipalities?
mcqs.explanation: Article 243C provides that the State Legislature regulates the composition of Panchayats and Municipalities.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The minimum qualifying age for Panchayats and Municipalities is 21 years.
Reason (R): Articles 243C and 243R deal with composition and age-related provisions for Panchayats and Municipalities.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The notes associate Articles 243C and 243R with composition and state that the minimum qualifying age for both bodies is 21 years.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Article 243D concerns reservations in Panchayats.
II. Article 243T concerns reservations in Municipalities.
III. Reservation for women is not less than one-third of total seats and chairpersons.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Articles 243D and 243T provide for reservations in Panchayats and Municipalities respectively, including reservation of at least one-third for women.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding reservation in local bodies?
options: The minimum reservation for women is less than one-third of total seats.
Articles 243D and 243T deal with reservations in Panchayats and Municipalities respectively.
Reservation for women also applies to chairpersons.
Reservation for women applies to not less than one-third of total seats.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement changes the prescribed extent. Reservation for women is not less than one-third, or at least 33%, of total seats and chairpersons.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding premature dissolution of a local body:
I. Elections must ordinarily be held within six months of dissolution.
II. Elections are not required if the remaining term is less than six months.
III. The fixed term of a local body is seven years.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. The fixed term is five years, not seven years, and the six-month exception applies when the remaining term is less than six months.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. A Panchayat has a fixed term of five years.
2. A Municipality has a fixed term of five years.
3. Elections after premature dissolution must always be held even when the remaining term is less than six months.
4. Articles 243E and 243U concern tenure and dissolution.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because elections are not required when the remaining term is less than six months.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Article 243D
(b) Article 243E
(c) Article 243G
(d) Article 243I

List-II
(i) Powers and responsibilities of Panchayats
(ii) Reservations in Panchayats
(iii) State Finance Commission
(iv) Tenure and dissolution of Panchayats
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are 243D–reservations, 243E–tenure and dissolution, 243G–powers and responsibilities, and 243I–State Finance Commission.

mcqs.question: At what interval is the State Finance Commission constituted to review local finance distribution?
mcqs.explanation: The State Finance Commission is constituted every five years by the Governor to review local finance distribution.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The State Finance Commission for local bodies is constituted by the Governor.
Reason (R): It reviews the distribution of local finances.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the review of local finance distribution describes the Commission’s function; it does not explain why the Governor constitutes it.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the functional domain of local self-government?
options: Local bodies may deal with roads and bridges.
Local bodies may deal with economic development and social justice.
Local bodies may deal with sanitation and public health.
Judicial review is a local-government functional subject.
mcqs.explanation: Judicial review is not a local-government functional subject. The listed local functions include economic development, social justice, sanitation, public health, and roads and bridges.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Powers and responsibilities of Panchayats are addressed in Article 243G.
II. Powers and responsibilities of Municipalities are addressed in Article 243W.
III. Water supply and local utilities fall within the listed local-government functions.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Articles 243G and 243W concern Panchayat and Municipality powers respectively, including functions such as water supply and local utilities.

mcqs.question: Which Article deals with the powers and responsibilities of Municipalities?
mcqs.explanation: Article 243W deals with the powers and responsibilities of Municipalities.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Article 243-Y concerns the State Finance Commission for Municipalities.
Statement B: Article 243-I concerns the State Finance Commission for Panchayats.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The notes pair Article 243-I with Panchayats and Article 243-Y with Municipalities for State Finance Commission provisions.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Article 243W
(b) Article 243Y
(c) Article 243Z
(d) Article 243ZE

List-II
(i) Metropolitan Planning Committee
(ii) Accounts and audit of Municipalities
(iii) State Finance Commission for Municipalities
(iv) Powers and responsibilities of Municipalities
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Article 243W–Municipality powers, 243Y–State Finance Commission, 243Z–accounts and audit, and 243ZE–Metropolitan Planning Committee.

mcqs.question: Under which enactment was Local Self-Government made a Transferred Subject under provincial dyarchy?
mcqs.explanation: The Government of India Act, 1919 made Local Self-Government a Transferred Subject under provincial dyarchy.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Local self-government is not central control.
Statement B: Local self-government is not mere administration.
