II. Such extension can continue beyond six months after the Emergency ceases.
III. Laws made by Parliament on State List subjects cease to operate six months after the Emergency is revoked.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and III are correct. Legislative terms may be extended one year at a time, but only up to a maximum of six months after the Emergency ceases.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Feature)
a. Article 358
b. Article 359
c. Articles 20 and 21

List-II (Description)
i. Cannot be suspended under any circumstances
 ii. Requires a specific, separate Presidential Order
 iii. Automatic suspension upon proclamation
mcqs.explanation: Article 358 operates automatically upon proclamation, Article 359 requires a separate Presidential Order, and Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended under any circumstances.

mcqs.keyword: President's Rule – Extension Beyond One Year
mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): President’s Rule can be extended beyond one year only when two specified conditions are satisfied.
Reason (R): A National Emergency must be in operation in the whole of India or in any part of the concerned State, and the Election Commission must certify that elections cannot be held.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the two conditions stated in the Reason explain the basis for extending President’s Rule beyond one year, subject to the three-year cap.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. National Emergency invoked in 1975
B. National Emergency invoked in 1962
C. National Emergency formally withdrawn on 21 March 1977
D. National Emergency invoked in 1971
mcqs.explanation: The correct sequence is 1962, 1971, 1975 and 21 March 1977: B, D, A, C.

mcqs.question: Which change was made by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978 under Article 352?
options: Approval time for National Emergency was increased from one month to two months
The requirement of written advice from the Union Cabinet was removed
mcqs.explanation: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 replaced “Internal Disturbance” with “Armed Rebellion” as a ground under Article 352.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the 44th Amendment Act, 1978:
I. It reduced the parliamentary approval period for National Emergency from two months to one month.
II. It guaranteed that enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended under Article 359.
III. It required the President to proclaim National Emergency only upon written advice of the Union Cabinet.
IV. It changed “Internal Disturbance” to “Armed Rebellion” under Article 352.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements describe landmarks of the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. National Emergency requires a special majority in both Houses.
2. President’s Rule requires a simple majority in both Houses.
3. Financial Emergency requires a simple majority in both Houses.
4. National Emergency has a maximum continuation limit of three years.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. National Emergency may continue six months at a time with no maximum limit specified in the comparison, so statement 4 is incorrect.

mcqs.question: Emergency provisions in the Constitution are governed under which Part?
mcqs.explanation: Emergency provisions are placed in Part XVIII of the Constitution, covering Articles 352 to 360.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)
a. Article 352
b. Article 356
c. Article 360

List-II (Constitutional provision)
i. Financial Emergency
ii. National Emergency
iii. President's Rule

Codes:
mcqs.explanation: Article 352 concerns National Emergency, Article 356 concerns President's Rule, and Article 360 concerns Financial Emergency.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The President may impose President's Rule on the report of the Governor or otherwise.
Statement B: President's Rule is imposed when the government of a State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Article 356 permits action on the Governor's report or otherwise, when the State government cannot be carried on constitutionally.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A Financial Emergency continues until it is revoked by the President.
Reason (R): The Financial Emergency provision prescribes a fixed maximum continuation period of three years.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: A is true because a Financial Emergency continues until revoked by the President. R is false: the three-year maximum applies to President's Rule, not Financial Emergency.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Parliamentary approval for President's Rule requires a simple majority in both Houses.
II. Parliamentary approval for Financial Emergency requires a simple majority in both Houses.
III. Parliamentary approval for National Emergency requires a simple majority in both Houses.
mcqs.explanation: President's Rule and Financial Emergency require a simple majority in both Houses. National Emergency requires a special majority.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Emergency)
a. National Emergency
b. President's Rule
c. Financial Emergency

a List-II (Continuation provision)
i. Six months at a time, with no maximum limit
ii. Six months at a time, subject to a maximum of three years
iii. Continues until revoked by the President

Codes:
mcqs.explanation: National Emergency continues six months at a time without a maximum limit; President's Rule has a three-year maximum; Financial Emergency continues until revoked.

mcqs.question: When President's Rule is in operation, who passes the State Budget?
mcqs.explanation: Under President's Rule, the State Assembly is dissolved or suspended and Parliament passes the State Budget.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): During a Financial Emergency, salaries may be reduced even in the case of Supreme Court and High Court judges.
Reason (R): A Financial Emergency permits the executive to give financial directions.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The financial directions permitted during a Financial Emergency include the power to reduce salaries, including those of Supreme Court and High Court judges.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. A dissolved Lok Sabha survives for 30 days from the first sitting of the new Lok Sabha during a National Emergency.
II. A dissolved Lok Sabha survives for 30 days from the first sitting of the new Lok Sabha during President's Rule.
III. A dissolved Lok Sabha survives for 30 days from the first sitting of the new Lok Sabha during a Financial Emergency.
mcqs.explanation: The table specifies a 30-day survival from the first sitting of the new Lok Sabha for a dissolved Lok Sabha under all three types of Emergency.

mcqs.question: During a National Emergency, for how long may Parliament extend the term of the Lok Sabha or a State Assembly at a time by law?
mcqs.explanation: Parliament may extend the term of the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies by law for one year at a time during a National Emergency.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: An extension of the term of a Lok Sabha or State Assembly during a National Emergency may continue only up to six months after the Emergency ceases.
Statement B: Laws made by Parliament on State List subjects during a National Emergency cease to operate six months after the Emergency is revoked.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements reflect the specified post-Emergency limits: legislative-term extensions last up to six months after the Emergency ceases, and State List laws cease six months after revocation.

mcqs.question: Under Article 354, what may the President modify during a National Emergency?
options: The constitutional distribution of revenues between the Union and States
The composition of the Election Commission
The tenure of Supreme Court judges
mcqs.explanation: Article 354 empowers the President to modify the constitutional distribution of revenues between the Union and the States.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the power under Article 354?
options: It is exercised by the President during a National Emergency.
It permanently changes the constitutional distribution of revenues between the Union and States.
It relates to modification of the distribution of revenues between the Union and States.
The modification remains valid up to the end of the financial year in which the proclamation ceases.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is 'permanently'. The modification remains valid only up to the end of the financial year in which the proclamation ceases.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Feature)
a. Article 358
b. Article 359
c. Articles 20 and 21

a List-II (Description)
i. Enforcement cannot be suspended under Article 359
ii. Automatically suspends the six basic freedoms under Article 19
iii. Suspends the right to approach courts for enforcement of specified Fundamental Rights

Codes:
mcqs.explanation: Article 358 automatically suspends the six Article 19 freedoms; Article 359 suspends access to courts for specified Fundamental Rights; Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended under Article 359.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Article 358 does not operate during a proclamation of Emergency on the ground of armed rebellion.
Reason (R): Article 358 operates only on the grounds of war or external aggression.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Since Article 358 operates only during an Emergency based on war or external aggression, it does not operate during an armed-rebellion proclamation.

mcqs.question: Unlike the automatic operation of Article 358, what does Article 359 require?
options: A special majority in the State Assembly
A specific and separate Presidential Order
A resolution of every State Legislature
A certificate from the Election Commission
mcqs.explanation: Article 359 requires a specific, separate Presidential Order to suspend the right to approach courts for enforcement of specified Fundamental Rights.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the 44th Amendment Act, 1978:
I. It replaced 'Internal Disturbance' with 'Armed Rebellion' under Article 352.
II. It reduced the parliamentary approval period for National Emergency from two months to one month.
III. It required the President to proclaim National Emergency only upon written advice of the Union Cabinet.
mcqs.explanation: All three are listed as landmarks of the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.

mcqs.question: On which date was the 1975 Emergency proclaimed?
mcqs.explanation: The 1975 Emergency was proclaimed on 25 June 1975 on the ground of Internal Disturbance.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. Article 358 automatically suspends the six basic freedoms under Article 19.
2. Article 359 requires a specific, separate Presidential Order.
3. Articles 20 and 21 can be suspended during an armed rebellion proclamation.
4. Article 358 operates on the ground of armed rebellion.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statements 3 and 4 are incorrect: Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended, and Article 358 operates only on war or external aggression, not armed rebellion.

mcqs.question: Under the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, on whose written advice can the President proclaim a National Emergency?
options: The Governor of the concerned State
mcqs.explanation: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 added the requirement that the President can proclaim a National Emergency only upon the written advice of the Union Cabinet.

mcqs.question: On which date was the Emergency of 1975 formally withdrawn?
mcqs.explanation: The 1975 Emergency was proclaimed on 25 June 1975 and formally withdrawn on 21 March 1977.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding Parliament’s legislative powers during a National Emergency?
options: Laws made by Parliament on State List subjects cease to operate six months after the Emergency is revoked.
The power concerns laws made during the operation of a National Emergency.
Parliamentary laws on State List subjects continue permanently even after the Emergency is revoked.
Parliament acquires overriding legislative jurisdiction over subjects in the State List.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that such laws continue permanently. Laws made by Parliament on State List subjects cease to operate six months after the Emergency is revoked.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Article 359 operates during both an External Emergency and an Internal Emergency based on Armed Rebellion.
Reason (R): Article 359 requires a specific, separate Presidential Order.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Article 359 operates during both External Emergency and Internal Emergency based on Armed Rebellion, and it requires a specific Presidential Order. The requirement of a separate order does not explain its applicability to both grounds.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: During a National Emergency, the President may modify the constitutional distribution of revenues between the Union and the States.
Statement B: Such modification remains valid up to the end of the financial year in which the proclamation of Emergency ceases.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Article 354 empowers the President to modify the constitutional distribution of revenues between the Union and the States. The modification may remain valid up to the end of the financial year in which the proclamation ceases.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the 44th Amendment Act, 1978:
I. It required written advice of the Union Cabinet for the proclamation of a National Emergency.
II. It replaced the expression ‘Internal Disturbance’ with ‘Armed Rebellion’ under Article 352.
III. It guaranteed that enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended under Article 359.
IV. It permitted enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 to be suspended during an Armed Rebellion.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct changes associated with the 44th Amendment. Statement IV is incorrect because enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended under Article 359.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Proclamation of National Emergency
 b. Laws made by Parliament on State List subjects
 c. Modification of revenue distribution by the President
 d. Proclamation of Emergency in 1975

List-II
 i. Valid up to the end of the financial year in which the proclamation ceases
 ii. Made on 25 June 1975
 iii. Requires written advice of the Union Cabinet
 iv. Cease to operate six months after revocation of the Emergency
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-iii, b-iv, c-i and d-ii. A National Emergency requires written Cabinet advice; State List laws cease six months after revocation; revenue modification lasts up to the end of the relevant financial year; and the 1975 Emergency was proclaimed on 25 June.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following were changes or safeguards associated with the 44th Amendment Act, 1978?

1. Replacement of ‘Internal Disturbance’ with ‘Armed Rebellion’
2. Requirement of written advice of the Union Cabinet
3. Guarantee that Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended
4. Reduction of the approval period for National Emergency from two months to one month
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are associated with the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, as described in the emergency provisions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
options: It may be proclaimed when the financial stability or credit of India or any part of it is threatened.
Salaries may be reduced, including those of Supreme Court and High Court judges.
The executive may give financial directions during its operation.
It automatically ends after a fixed maximum period of three years.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that a Financial Emergency automatically ends after three years. It continues until revoked by the President and has no prescribed fixed maximum period.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: President’s Rule does not directly suspend Fundamental Rights.
Statement B: A Financial Emergency does not directly suspend Fundamental Rights.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Under the comparison of emergencies, neither President’s Rule under Article 356 nor Financial Emergency under Article 360 directly suspends Fundamental Rights.

mcqs.question: What does Judicial Review primarily empower the higher judiciary to do?
options: Examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders
Hear only ordinary appeals from lower courts
Review the political wisdom of every legislative policy
Grant automatic pre-assent to all Bills
mcqs.explanation: Judicial Review is the inherent constitutional power of the higher judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders, declaring them void when they contravene constitutional provisions.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding constitutional provisions:

List-I
(a) Article 13(2)
(b) Article 32
(c) Article 226
(d) Article 137

List-II
(i) High Court writ jurisdiction for Fundamental Rights and any other legal right
(ii) Supreme Court power to review its own judgments or orders
(iii) Laws abridging Fundamental Rights are void pro tanto
(iv) Supreme Court writ jurisdiction for enforcement of Fundamental Rights
mcqs.explanation: Article 13(2) is the primary textual foundation for striking down laws abridging Fundamental Rights; Articles 32 and 226 concern Supreme Court and High Court writ jurisdiction respectively; Article 137 concerns review of the Supreme Court’s own judgments or orders.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: India follows constitutional supremacy with Judicial Review.
The UK has no traditional judicial review of primary parliamentary legislation.
India follows parliamentary sovereignty instead of constitutional supremacy.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement alters India’s constitutional arrangement. India follows constitutional supremacy with Judicial Review, whereas the UK is described as following parliamentary sovereignty.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Judicial Review is exercised jointly by the Supreme Court and the High Courts.
Reason (R): Article 32 vests writ jurisdiction in the Supreme Court, while Article 226 vests writ jurisdiction in the High Courts.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 32 concerns the Supreme Court’s writ jurisdiction and Article 226 concerns the High Courts’ writ jurisdiction, together explaining the joint exercise of Judicial Review.

mcqs.question: Judicial Review was adopted from which country?
mcqs.explanation: The notes identify the USA as the borrowed source of Judicial Review.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Minerva Mills reaffirmed Judicial Review as part of the Basic Structure
B. Judicial Review originated in Marbury v. Madison
C. The First Constitutional Amendment added the Ninth Schedule
D. Kesavananda Bharati declared Judicial Review under Articles 32 and 226 integral to the Basic Structure
mcqs.explanation: The correct sequence is Marbury v. Madison (1803), the First Constitutional Amendment (1951), Kesavananda Bharati (1973), and Minerva Mills (1980).

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Article 13(2) is the primary textual foundation for striking down ultra vires laws.
II. Article 32 is described as part of the Basic Structure.
III. Article 142 is the provision for the Supreme Court’s review of its own judgments.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. Article 137, not Article 142, concerns the Supreme Court’s power to review its own judgments; Article 142 concerns complete justice.

mcqs.question: Which Article empowers the Supreme Court to pass decrees or orders for ‘Complete Justice’?
mcqs.explanation: Article 142 gives the Supreme Court the power to pass decrees or orders for ‘Complete Justice’ and is described as an inherent equitable jurisdiction distinct from Judicial Review.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Article 226 has a wider writ scope than Article 32.
Statement B: Article 226 concerns writ jurisdiction only for Fundamental Rights and not for any other legal right.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true because Article 226 covers Fundamental Rights and any other legal right. Statement B is false because it incorrectly excludes other legal rights.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Parliament cannot abrogate Judicial Review under Articles 32 and 226 even through Article 368.
Reason (R): Judicial Review under Articles 32 and 226 was declared an integral part of the Basic Structure.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the Reason explains the Assertion. Since Judicial Review under Articles 32 and 226 is part of the Basic Structure, Parliament cannot abrogate it even through Article 368.

mcqs.question:
Match the case with the associated proposition:

List-I
(a) Kesavananda Bharati (1973)
(b) Minerva Mills (1980)
(c) Marbury v. Madison (1803)
(d) First Constitutional Amendment (1951)

List-II
(i) Added the Ninth Schedule along with Articles 31A and 31B
(ii) Origin of Judicial Review
(iii) Declared Judicial Review under Articles 32 and 226 integral to the Basic Structure
(iv) Reaffirmed the Basic Structure status of Judicial Review
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Kesavananda Bharati—integral Basic Structure status, Minerva Mills—reaffirmation, Marbury v. Madison—origin of Judicial Review, and the First Constitutional Amendment—Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule.

mcqs.question: What was the principal purpose of adding Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule through the First Constitutional Amendment?
options: To insulate agrarian and land-reform laws from Judicial Review on Fundamental Rights grounds
To provide automatic pre-assent scrutiny of Bills
To establish parliamentary sovereignty over the Constitution
To create the Supreme Court’s power of review under Article 137
mcqs.explanation: The First Constitutional Amendment added Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule to insulate agrarian and land-reform laws from Judicial Review on Fundamental Rights grounds.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are expressly identified as things Judicial Review is NOT?
1. Questioning the political wisdom of legislation
2. Automatic pre-assent scrutiny of Bills
3. An ordinary appellate proceeding
4. Examining the constitutionality of executive orders
mcqs.explanation: The first three are expressly identified as things Judicial Review is not. Examining the constitutionality of executive orders is part of Judicial Review, so three statements qualify.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The First Constitutional Amendment was enacted in 1951.
II. It added Articles 31A and 31B.
III. It added the Ninth Schedule.
IV. It was enacted largely to overcome early judicial interpretations restricting state welfare and land-acquisition measures.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. The First Constitutional Amendment of 1951 added Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule and was largely intended to overcome early restrictive judicial interpretations affecting welfare and land-acquisition measures.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Judicial Review reinforces the federal principle.
Statement B: Judicial Review is classified as a unitary element of the Constitution.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true because Judicial Review preserves the constitutional distribution of powers and enforces constitutional limits. Statement B is false; the notes specifically distinguish it from unitary elements.

mcqs.question:
Match the concept with the correct description:

List-I
(a) Constitutional supremacy in India
(b) Parliamentary sovereignty in the UK
(c) Judicial Review as a federal principle
(d) Article 142 jurisdiction

List-II
(i) Power to pass decrees or orders for Complete Justice
(ii) Preserves distribution of powers and enforces constitutional limits
(iii) No traditional Judicial Review of primary parliamentary legislation
(iv) Constitutional supremacy with Judicial Review

Options:
mcqs.explanation: India is associated with constitutional supremacy and Judicial Review; the UK with parliamentary sovereignty and no traditional review of primary parliamentary legislation; Judicial Review reinforces federalism; and Article 142 concerns Complete Justice.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Judicial Review is not an ordinary appellate proceeding.
Reason (R): Judicial Review examines constitutional validity rather than merely reconsidering a case through an ordinary appeal.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the Reason explains the Assertion. Judicial Review concerns constitutional validity and is expressly distinguished from an ordinary appellate proceeding.

mcqs.question: Which judicial decision originated Judicial Review, according to the stated constitutional source?
mcqs.explanation: Judicial Review is stated to have originated in Marbury v. Madison (1803), decided by Chief Justice John Marshall.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following Article-provision pairs are correctly matched?
1. Article 13(2)—laws abridging Fundamental Rights are void pro tanto
2. Article 32—Supreme Court writ jurisdiction for Fundamental Rights enforcement
3. Article 226—High Court writ jurisdiction for Fundamental Rights and any other legal right
4. Article 137—Supreme Court power to review its own judgments or orders
mcqs.explanation: All four pairs are correctly matched. Articles 13(2), 32, 226 and 137 correspond respectively to the stated constitutional bases and powers.

mcqs.question: Which constitutional provision empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgments or orders?
mcqs.explanation: Article 137 confers upon the Supreme Court the power to review its own judgments or orders.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the constitutional significance of Article 13(2)?
options: It makes laws abridging Fundamental Rights void pro tanto
It provides the High Courts with writ jurisdiction for any legal right
It empowers the Supreme Court to pass orders for complete justice
It enables the Supreme Court to review its own judgments
mcqs.explanation: Article 13(2) is the primary textual foundation for declaring laws abridging Fundamental Rights void pro tanto.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Constitutional amendments are subject to Judicial Review.
Reason (R): Such amendments can be tested on the touchstone of the Basic Structure doctrine.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Constitutional amendments are subject to Judicial Review precisely because they may be examined against the Basic Structure doctrine.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Article 226 permits High Courts to exercise writ jurisdiction in matters involving Fundamental Rights as well as any other legal right.
Statement B: Article 226 has a wider writ scope than Article 32.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 226 covers Fundamental Rights and any other legal right, giving it a wider writ scope than Article 32.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The First Constitutional Amendment was enacted in 1951.
II. Articles 31A and 31B and the Ninth Schedule were added to insulate agrarian and land-reform laws from Judicial Review on Fundamental Rights grounds.
III. The amendment was enacted largely to overcome early judicial interpretations restricting state welfare and land-acquisition measures.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The First Constitutional Amendment of 1951 added Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule for the stated protective purpose.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Article 137
(b) Article 142
(c) Article 226
(d) Article 13(2)

List-II
(i) Laws abridging Fundamental Rights are void pro tanto
(ii) High Court writ jurisdiction for Fundamental Rights and any other legal right
(iii) Supreme Court's power to review its own judgments or orders
(iv) Power of the Supreme Court to pass decrees or orders for Complete Justice
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-iii, b-iv, c-ii and d-i. Article 137 concerns review of the Supreme Court's own orders, while Article 142 concerns Complete Justice.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Judicial Review reinforces the federal principle.
Reason (R): It preserves the constitutional distribution of powers and enforces constitutional limits.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. By preserving the constitutional distribution of powers and enforcing constitutional limits, Judicial Review reinforces the federal principle.

mcqs.question: The First Constitutional Amendment was enacted largely to overcome early judicial interpretations that restricted which measures?
options: The Supreme Court's power to review its own judgments
High Court writ jurisdiction and legal remedies
The power to pass decrees for Complete Justice
mcqs.explanation: The First Constitutional Amendment was enacted largely to overcome early judicial interpretations restricting state welfare and land-acquisition measures.

mcqs.question: Who was the Chief Justice associated with the origin of Judicial Review in Marbury v. Madison (1803)?
mcqs.explanation: Judicial Review originated in Marbury v. Madison (1803), decided by Chief Justice John Marshall.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Article 142 is distinct from Judicial Review.
Reason (R): Article 142 empowers the Supreme Court to pass decrees or orders for ‘Complete Justice’ and represents inherent equitable jurisdiction.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 142 deals with the Supreme Court’s power to secure ‘Complete Justice’ through its inherent equitable jurisdiction, rather than exercising Judicial Review.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Judicial Review does not involve the court questioning the advisability of legislation.
Reason (R): Judicial Review examines the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Judicial Review examines constitutional validity; it does not assess the political wisdom, policy merits or advisability of legislation.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are identified as unitary elements?
1. All India Services
2. Governor's appointment
3. Emergency provisions
4. Judicial Review
mcqs.explanation: Three are unitary elements: All India Services, the Governor's appointment and emergency provisions. Judicial Review reinforces the federal principle and is not a unitary element.

mcqs.question: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States?
options: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
mcqs.explanation: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under Articles 64 and 89(1).

mcqs.question: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
options: The Deputy Chairman is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
The Deputy Chairman is elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members.
The Deputy Chairman is chosen from among the sitting members of the Rajya Sabha.
The Deputy Chairman is nominated by the President from outside Parliament.
mcqs.explanation: Under Article 89(2), the Deputy Chairman is chosen from among the sitting members of the Rajya Sabha and is therefore a member of the House.

mcqs.question: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is elected by:
options: The Vice-President from among the members of Parliament
The Lok Sabha from among its members
The Rajya Sabha from among its members
The President from among the members of the Lok Sabha
mcqs.explanation: Article 93 provides that the Lok Sabha elects its Speaker from among its members.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Drafting Committee
(b) Union Constitution Committee
(c) Rules of Procedure Committee
(d) Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee

List-II
(i) J.B. Kripalani
(ii) Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
(iii) Dr. Rajendra Prasad
(iv) Jawaharlal Nehru
mcqs.explanation: The Drafting Committee was chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the Union Constitution Committee by Jawaharlal Nehru, the Rules of Procedure Committee by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, and the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee by J.B. Kripalani.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Advisory Committee on FRs, Minorities, Tribals
(b) Minorities Sub-Committee
(c) House Committee
(d) Finance & Staff Committee

List-II
(i) G.V. Mavalankar
(ii) H.C. Mukherjee
(iii) Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
(iv) Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar
mcqs.explanation: The respective chairpersons were Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, H.C. Mukherjee, G.V. Mavalankar and Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar.

mcqs.question: The Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly, chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, was constituted on:
mcqs.explanation: The Drafting Committee was constituted on 29 August 1947. It had seven members and prepared the draft Constitution.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Union Powers Committee was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru and dealt with federal subject distribution.
The Steering Committee was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad and dealt with steering Assembly business.
The States-Related Committee was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and dealt with provincial constitutional framework.
The Constituent Assembly Functions Committee was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru and dealt with the operational functions of the Assembly.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the chairperson and subject. The States-Related Committee was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad and dealt with negotiations with Princely States; the provincial constitutional framework was handled by the Provincial Constitution Committee chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Since 1967, the Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee has conventionally been selected from the Opposition.
Reason (R): The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Speaker appoints the PAC Chairman, while selection from the Opposition is a convention since 1967; the appointment does not explain that convention.

mcqs.question: What is the composition of the Public Accounts Committee?
options: 30 members from the Lok Sabha only
22 members: 7 from the Lok Sabha and 15 from the Rajya Sabha
20 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 5 from the Rajya Sabha
22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
mcqs.explanation: The Public Accounts Committee has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.question: Which parliamentary committee has 30 members drawn from the Lok Sabha only and is the largest parliamentary committee?
mcqs.explanation: The Estimates Committee has 30 members from the Lok Sabha only and is the largest parliamentary committee.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the Committee on Public Undertakings is incorrect?
options: Its Chairman is conventionally selected from the Opposition since 1967.
It has 15 members from the Lok Sabha and 7 members from the Rajya Sabha.
Its Chairman is appointed by the Speaker.
mcqs.explanation: The altered detail is the convention about selection from the Opposition. That convention since 1967 relates to the Public Accounts Committee; the Chairman of the Committee on Public Undertakings is appointed by the Speaker.

mcqs.question:
Match the body with the authority that appoints its Chairman or members.

List-I
(a) UPSC
(b) State PSC
(c) Finance Commission
(d) Lokpal Selection Committee

List-II
(i) Governor of the State
(ii) President of India
(iii) Prime Minister
(iv) Parliament by law
mcqs.explanation: The President appoints the UPSC and Finance Commission, the Governor appoints the State PSC, and the Prime Minister chairs the Lokpal Selection Committee. Parliament prescribes Finance Commission qualifications by law, but does not appoint it.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): An SPSC Chairman appointed by the Governor can be removed only by the President.
Reason (R): Removal for misbehavior under Article 317 requires a binding Supreme Court inquiry.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the Article 317 requirement of a binding Supreme Court inquiry explains why removal is by the President rather than the Governor.

mcqs.question: The first Chairman of the Finance Commission was:
mcqs.explanation: The notes identify K.C. Neogy as the first Chairman of the Finance Commission.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Commission:
I. It consists of five members, including the Chairman.
II. The President appoints the Chairman and members.
III. Parliament prescribes their qualifications by law.
IV. The Finance Commission has 22 members, comprising 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members, while the 22-member composition belongs to the Public Accounts Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings.

mcqs.question: Who chairs the Lokpal Selection Committee?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
mcqs.explanation: The Prime Minister is the Chairperson of the Lokpal Selection Committee.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the Lokpal Selection Committee is incorrect?
options: The Prime Minister is its Chairperson.
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is a member.
The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a member.
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is a member.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that the Rajya Sabha Chairman is a member. The listed members include the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, a CJI or Supreme Court Judge nominee, and an eminent jurist.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Estimates Committee is traditionally chaired by a member from the ruling party.
Statement B: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Estimates Committee Chairman is traditionally from the ruling party, and the PAC Chairman is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Governor appoints the Chairman of a State PSC.
Statement B: The Governor can remove the Chairman of a State PSC without the President's approval.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true, but Statement B is false. Although the Governor appoints the SPSC Chairman, only the President can remove the Chairman under Article 317.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following committees were chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad?
1. Ad-hoc Committee on National Flag
2. States-Related Committee
3. Rules of Procedure Committee
4. Steering Committee
mcqs.explanation: All four listed committees were chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad. The Ad-hoc Committee on National Flag was constituted on 23 June 1947.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Union Powers Committee
(b) Constituent Assembly Functions Committee
(c) Provincial Constitution Committee
(d) Order of Business Committee

List-II
(i) Provincial constitutional framework
(ii) Federal subject distribution
(iii) Day-to-day legislative agenda
(iv) Operational functions of the Assembly
mcqs.explanation: The Union Powers Committee dealt with federal subject distribution; the Constituent Assembly Functions Committee with operational functions; the Provincial Constitution Committee with the provincial constitutional framework; and the Order of Business Committee with the day-to-day legislative agenda.

mcqs.question: The ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States is provided under which combination of Articles?
mcqs.explanation: The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under Articles 64 and 89(1).

mcqs.question: Who chaired the Union Constitution Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
mcqs.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru chaired the Union Constitution Committee, which dealt with union constitutional powers.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Union Powers Committee dealt with the distribution of federal subjects.
Reason (R): It was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but Nehru’s chairmanship does not explain the committee’s subject-matter responsibility.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Constituent Assembly Functions Committee dealt with the operational functions of the Assembly.
Statement B: The Rules of Procedure Committee dealt with the Assembly’s procedural rules.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The Constituent Assembly Functions Committee handled operational functions, while the Rules of Procedure Committee handled procedural rules.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Constituent Assembly Functions Committee
(b) Rules of Procedure Committee
(c) Steering Committee
(d) Order of Business Committee

List-II
(i) K.M. Munshi
(ii) Dr. Rajendra Prasad
(iii) Jawaharlal Nehru
(iv) Dr. Rajendra Prasad
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Functions Committee–Nehru, Rules of Procedure–Rajendra Prasad, Steering Committee–Rajendra Prasad, and Order of Business–K.M. Munshi.

mcqs.question: The Ad-hoc Committee on National Flag was constituted on:
mcqs.explanation: The Ad-hoc Committee on National Flag is dated 23 June 1947.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribals was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
II. The Provincial Constitution Committee was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
III. The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee was chaired by H.C. Mukherjee.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee was chaired by J.B. Kripalani, not H.C. Mukherjee.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee
(b) Minorities Sub-Committee
(c) House Committee
(d) Finance & Staff Committee

List-II
(i) G.V. Mavalankar
(ii) H.C. Mukherjee
(iii) J.B. Kripalani
(iv) Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee–J.B. Kripalani, Minorities Sub-Committee–H.C. Mukherjee, House Committee–G.V. Mavalankar, and Finance & Staff Committee–Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar.

mcqs.question: Who was the chairperson of the Provincial Constitution Committee?
mcqs.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee.

mcqs.question: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the:
mcqs.explanation: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members.
Statement B: The Committee on Public Undertakings consists of 15 members from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members, comprising 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements about parliamentary committees are correct?
1. The Public Accounts Committee has 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha members.
2. The Estimates Committee has members from the Lok Sabha only.
3. The Committee on Public Undertakings has 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha members.
4. The Estimates Committee has 22 members.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect because the Estimates Committee has 30 members.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The qualifications of Finance Commission members are not prescribed by the President.
Reason (R): Parliament determines those qualifications by law.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the parliamentary prescription of qualifications explains why they are not prescribed by the President. The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280.

mcqs.question: The qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission are prescribed by:
mcqs.explanation: Although the President appoints the Chairman and members, Parliament determines their qualifications by law under the Finance Commission framework.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) UPSC
(b) State PSC
(c) Finance Commission
(d) Lokpal Selection Committee

List-II
(i) Article 280
(ii) Article 315
(iii) Article 317 governs removal for misbehavior
(iv) Prime Minister as Chairperson
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are UPSC–Article 315, State PSC–Article 317 for removal for misbehavior, Finance Commission–Article 280, and Lokpal Selection Committee–Prime Minister as Chairperson.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the Lokpal Selection Committee:
I. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is a member.
II. The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a member.
III. A Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge nominated by the Chief Justice of India is a member.
IV. An eminent jurist is a member.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct components of the Lokpal Selection Committee. The Prime Minister is its Chairperson.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The President appoints and removes the Chairperson of the Union Public Service Commission.
Reason (R): Removal for misbehavior requires a binding inquiry by the Supreme Court under Article 317.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: The President appoints and removes the UPSC Chairperson. However, the Supreme Court inquiry requirement explains the removal procedure for misbehavior, not the President’s appointing power; hence both statements are true, but R does not correctly explain A.

mcqs.question: The 1931 Karachi Congress Flag Committee was chaired by:
mcqs.explanation: The 1931 Karachi Congress Flag Committee was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. This is distinct from the 1947 Constituent Assembly Ad-hoc Committee on National Flag, which was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Drafting Committee consisted of seven members.
Reason (R): The Drafting Committee prepared the draft Constitution.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: the Drafting Committee had seven members and prepared the draft Constitution. However, its preparation of the draft Constitution does not explain why it had seven members.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribals was the parent overarching advisory committee.
Statement B: The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee dealt with the detailed formulation of fundamental rights.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. The Advisory Committee was the parent overarching advisory committee, while the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee handled the detailed formulation of fundamental rights.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Minorities Sub-Committee dealt with minority safeguards.
II. The House Committee dealt with residential and Assembly accommodations.
III. The Finance and Staff Committee dealt with internal staff and budget matters.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. These committees respectively dealt with minority safeguards, residential and Assembly accommodations, and internal staff and budget matters.

mcqs.question: Who appoints the Chairman of the Estimates Committee?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
mcqs.explanation: The Chairman of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

mcqs.question: Which Constituent Assembly committee dealt with Union constitutional powers?
mcqs.explanation: The Union Constitution Committee, chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru, dealt with Union constitutional powers. The Union Powers Committee dealt with the distribution of federal subjects.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Finance Commission Chairperson has a fixed statutory term.
Statement B: The qualifications of the Finance Commission Chairperson and members are prescribed by the President.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true: the Finance Commission Chairperson has a fixed statutory term. Statement B is false because Parliament, by law, determines the qualifications of the Chairperson and members.

53.title: Representation of People Acts and Electoral Reforms

mcqs.question: Which of the following is primarily dealt with by the Representation of the People Act, 1950?
options: Registration of political parties and corrupt practices
Conduct of elections and election petitions
Allocation of seats, delimitation of constituencies and preparation of electoral rolls
mcqs.explanation: The RPA, 1950 deals with allocation of seats, delimitation, voter qualifications and preparation of electoral rolls. The operational conduct of elections and candidature are mainly covered by the RPA, 1951.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The RPA, 1950 deals with the detailed composition of State Legislative Councils.
The RPA, 1950 deals with corrupt practices during elections.
The RPA, 1951 deals with the registration of political parties.
The RPA, 1951 deals with election petitions and disputes.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is attributing corrupt practices to the RPA, 1950. Corrupt practices are dealt with by the RPA, 1951.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Political parties are registered by the Election Commission of India.
Reason (R): Section 29A of the RPA, 1951 provides for registration of political parties.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The ECI registers political parties under Section 29A of the RPA, 1951.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The right to vote is a Fundamental Right.
Statement B: The right to contest an election is a statutory right.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The right to vote and the right to contest are legal or statutory rights, not Fundamental Rights, as upheld in Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India (2006).

mcqs.question:
Which of the following statements are correct?
I. The RPA, 1950 is connected with Articles 81, 82, 170, 171, 325 and 326.
II. The RPA, 1951 is connected with Articles 84, 102, 173, 191, 324 and 329.
III. Article 329 is listed as a constitutional connection of the RPA, 1950.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. Article 329 is listed with the RPA, 1951, not with the RPA, 1950.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) RPA, 1950
(b) RPA, 1951
(c) Section 29A
(d) Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968

List-II
(i) Recognition of National and State parties
(ii) Registration of political parties
(iii) Pre-election framework and voter rolls
(iv) Operational conduct of elections and candidature
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: RPA, 1950—pre-election framework and voter rolls; RPA, 1951—operational conduct and candidature; Section 29A—party registration; 1968 Order—party recognition.

mcqs.question: Under Section 33(7) of the RPA, 1951, a candidate may contest simultaneously from a maximum of how many Parliamentary or Assembly constituencies?
mcqs.explanation: Section 33(7) permits a candidate to contest from a maximum of two Parliamentary or two Assembly constituencies at a time.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A registered elector in India can contest a Rajya Sabha election from any State.
Reason (R): The 2003 Amendment removed the requirement that the candidate be an elector in the particular State.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The 2003 Amendment removed the State-specific elector requirement, and this position was upheld by the Supreme Court in Kuldip Nayar (2006).

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the death of a contesting candidate?
options: The election is automatically cancelled in every case of the death of a candidate.
The death of a candidate no longer automatically countermands the election.
The change was made through the 1996 Amendment.
Recognized political parties may nominate a replacement within a set timeframe.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that the election is automatically cancelled in every such case. After the 1996 Amendment, recognized political parties may nominate a replacement within a set timeframe.

mcqs.question: The Dinesh Goswami Committee, set up in 1990, was associated with which subject?
mcqs.explanation: The Dinesh Goswami Committee was set up in 1990 on electoral reforms. It recommended state funding of elections and EVMs, among other measures.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Delimitation Commission
(b) Retired Supreme Court Judge
(c) Chief Election Commissioner
(d) State Election Commissions

List-II
(i) One component of the Commission
(ii) One component of the Commission
(iii) Head of the Commission
(iv) One component of the Commission
mcqs.explanation: The Delimitation Commission is headed by a retired Supreme Court Judge, with the CEC and State Election Commissions as other specified components.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be called in question in any court.
Reason (R): Article 329 gives finality to such orders, and once laid before Parliament or Assemblies they cannot be modified.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The notes specifically connect the finality of Delimitation Commission orders with Article 329 and state that the orders cannot be modified after being laid before the legislatures.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following Delimitation Commissions in chronological order:
A. 1973 Commission
B. 1952 Commission
C. 2002 Commission
D. 1963 Commission
mcqs.explanation: The four Delimitation Commissions were constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002. Therefore, the correct order is B, D, A, C.

mcqs.question: Where and when was VVPAT first used?
options: A Lok Sabha general election in 1996
mcqs.explanation: VVPAT was first used in the Noksen Assembly by-election in Nagaland in September 2013.

mcqs.question: The introduction of NOTA was directed by the Supreme Court on which date in PUCL v. Union of India?
mcqs.explanation: The Supreme Court directed the introduction of NOTA on 27 September 2013 in PUCL v. Union of India.

mcqs.question:
Which of the following are criteria for recognition as a National Party?
I. Securing at least 6% of total valid votes in four or more States and at least four Lok Sabha seats.
II. Winning at least 2% of the total Lok Sabha seats, with elected members from at least three States.
III. Being recognized as a State Party in at least four different States.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements state alternatives for National Party recognition given in the notes. The first requires the vote share and four Lok Sabha seats; the second requires 2% of Lok Sabha seats and representation from at least three States; the third requires State Party recognition in four States.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are stated alternatives for recognition as a National Party?
I. At least 6% of valid votes in four or more States plus at least four Lok Sabha seats.
II. At least 2% of Lok Sabha seats, with members from at least three States.
III. Recognition as a State Party in at least four States.
IV. Registration under Section 29A of the RPA, 1951.
mcqs.explanation: Only the first three are National Party recognition alternatives. Registration under Section 29A is the process for registering political parties, not an alternative recognition criterion.

mcqs.question: When does the Model Code of Conduct come into force?
options: Immediately upon the formal announcement of the election schedule by the ECI
After the completion of nomination and scrutiny
After Parliament approves the election schedule
When the election results are declared
mcqs.explanation: The Model Code of Conduct comes into force immediately upon the formal announcement of the election schedule by the Election Commission of India.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The RPA, 1950 contains the seat-quota and delimitation framework.
Statement B: The RPA, 1951 contains provisions concerning political party registration and corrupt practices.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Seat quotas and the delimitation framework belong to the RPA, 1950, while political party registration and corrupt practices are key operational provisions of the RPA, 1951.

mcqs.question: Which provision is specifically associated with the detailed composition of State Legislative Councils under the RPA, 1950?
options: Article 324, Section 33(7) and the Second Schedule
Article 329, Section 29A and the First Schedule
Article 326, Section 10 and the Fourth Schedule
Article 171(2), Section 10 and the Third Schedule
mcqs.explanation: The detailed composition of State Legislative Councils is linked with Article 171(2), Section 10 and the Third Schedule of the RPA, 1950.

mcqs.question: Which of the following procedures is specifically associated with the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
options: Detailed composition of State Legislative Councils
Nomination, scrutiny and counting of votes
mcqs.explanation: The RPA, 1951 deals with the operational conduct of elections, including nomination, scrutiny and counting procedures.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Representation of the People Act, 1950 deals with the registration of electors.
II. The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with disqualifications for holding membership.
III. The Representation of the People Act, 1950 deals with corrupt practices.
mcqs.explanation: Registration of electors belongs to the RPA, 1950, while disqualifications for holding membership belong to the RPA, 1951. Corrupt practices are dealt with by the RPA, 1951, so Statement III is false.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) RPA, 1950
(b) RPA, 1951
(c) Pre-election framework
(d) Operational conduct of elections

List-II
i. Nomination, scrutiny and counting
 ii. Seat quotas and delimitation framework
 iii. Voter rolls
 iv. Candidature and election procedures
mcqs.explanation: The RPA, 1950 is associated with seat quotas, delimitation and voter rolls. The RPA, 1951 covers nomination, scrutiny, counting and operational election procedures.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The ceiling on the number of constituencies from which a candidate may contest was introduced through an amendment to the RPA, 1951 in 1996.
Reason (R): The amendment followed the 1991 election in which Devi Lal contested from three Lok Sabha seats.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The 1996 amendment followed the 1991 instance of Devi Lal contesting from three Lok Sabha seats and capped simultaneous contests at two.

mcqs.question: Which amendment removed the requirement that a Rajya Sabha candidate must be an elector in the particular State from which the candidate contests?
mcqs.explanation: The 2003 Amendment removed the State-specific elector requirement for Rajya Sabha candidature.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Before the 2003 Amendment, a Rajya Sabha candidate had to be an elector in the particular State concerned.
Statement B: The change in the Rajya Sabha elector requirement was upheld by the Supreme Court in Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The 2003 Amendment removed the State-specific requirement, and the change was upheld by the Supreme Court in 2006 in Kuldip Nayar.

mcqs.question:
Which of the following recommendations were associated with the Dinesh Goswami Committee?
I. State funding of elections
II. Use of Electronic Voting Machines
III. Measures subsequently enacted in the 1996 RPA Amendment
IV. Allocation of State Legislative Council seats
mcqs.explanation: The Dinesh Goswami Committee was set up on electoral reforms and recommended state funding of elections, EVMs and measures later enacted in the 1996 RPA Amendment.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following were associated with the recommendations of the Dinesh Goswami Committee?
1. State funding of elections
2. Electronic Voting Machines
3. Measures later enacted in the 1996 RPA Amendment
4. Formation of State Election Commissions
mcqs.explanation: The first three were associated with the Dinesh Goswami Committee. Formation of State Election Commissions was not listed among its recommendations.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Delimitation Commission
(b) Chairperson
(c) Election-related member
(d) State-level members

List-II
i. Chief Election Commissioner
 ii. State Election Commissions
 iii. Constituted under an Act of Parliament
 iv. Retired Supreme Court Judge
mcqs.explanation: The Delimitation Commission is constituted under an Act of Parliament, headed by a retired Supreme Court Judge, and includes the Chief Election Commissioner and State Election Commissions.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Orders of the Delimitation Commission have the force of law.
Reason (R): Once laid before Parliament or the State Assemblies, such orders cannot be modified.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The notes separately state that delimitation orders have the force of law and that, after being laid before the legislatures, they cannot be modified; the second statement does not explain the first.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the orders of the Delimitation Commission is incorrect?
options: They have the force of law.
They cannot be called in question in any court.
They may be modified by Parliament after being laid before it.
Article 329 is associated with the finality of such orders.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that Parliament may modify the orders. Once laid before Parliament or the Assemblies, the orders cannot be modified.

mcqs.question: How many Delimitation Commissions had been constituted according to the stated electoral framework?
mcqs.explanation: The notes identify four Delimitation Commissions: those constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Delimitation Commission is constituted by the Central Government under an Act of Parliament.
Statement B: The Delimitation Commission is headed by a serving State Election Commissioner.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true. The Commission is headed by a retired Supreme Court Judge, not a serving State Election Commissioner, so Statement B is false.

mcqs.question: In which electoral event was VVPAT first used?
options: A Lok Sabha general election in 2014
The Noksen Assembly by-election in Nagaland
mcqs.explanation: VVPAT was first used in the Noksen Assembly by-election in Nagaland in September 2013.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the introduction of NOTA?
options: The direction was issued in PUCL v. Union of India.
It was introduced through the 1996 Amendment to the RPA, 1951.
The direction was issued on 27 September 2013.
It was directed by the Supreme Court.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the 1996 RPA Amendment. The Supreme Court directed the introduction of NOTA on 27 September 2013 in PUCL v. Union of India.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following alternatives for recognition as a National Party:
I. Recognition as a State Party in at least four different States.
II. Winning at least 2% of the total Lok Sabha seats, with elected members from at least three States.
III. Winning at least 6% of total valid votes in four or more States and at least four Lok Sabha seats.
IV. Winning at least 6% of total valid votes in one State and at least two Lok Sabha seats.
mcqs.explanation: The first three are stated alternatives for National Party recognition. The fourth alternative is not listed.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are stated alternatives for recognition as a National Party?
1. Recognition as a State Party in at least four States
2. At least 2% of total Lok Sabha seats with elected members from at least three States
3. At least 6% of valid votes in four or more States plus at least four Lok Sabha seats
4. At least 6% of valid votes in one State plus two Lok Sabha seats
mcqs.explanation: The first three are stated alternatives. The fourth is not an alternative given for National Party recognition.

mcqs.question: The Model Code of Conduct comes into force when the Election Commission of India:
mcqs.explanation: The Model Code of Conduct comes into force immediately upon the formal announcement of the election schedule by the ECI.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Model Code of Conduct becomes operative immediately upon the formal announcement of the election schedule.
Reason (R): Its operation is linked to the Election Commission's formal announcement of the election schedule.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the reason directly explains the assertion: the MCC comes into force immediately upon the ECI's formal announcement of the election schedule.

mcqs.question: The ceiling of two constituencies from which a candidate may contest at a time was introduced in the context of which earlier electoral event?
options: The constitution of the 2002 Delimitation Commission
The first use of VVPAT in the 2013 Nagaland by-election
Devi Lal contesting from three Lok Sabha seats in the 1991 elections
mcqs.explanation: The 1996 amendment to the RPA, 1951 followed the 1991 elections, in which Devi Lal contested from three Lok Sabha seats.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Delimitation Commission includes State Election Commissioners in its composition.
Reason (R): The Commission is headed by a retired Supreme Court Judge and also includes the Chief Election Commissioner.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. State Election Commissioners are members of the Commission, while the retired Supreme Court Judge and the Chief Election Commissioner form other parts of its composition; the Reason does not explain the Assertion.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding an alternative route for recognition as a National Party:
I. The party must win at least 2% of the total seats in the Lok Sabha.
II. This requirement corresponds to 11 Lok Sabha seats.
III. The elected members must come from at least four different States.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. The 2% requirement equals 11 Lok Sabha seats, and the elected members must come from at least three different States, not four.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Article 84
(b) Article 102
(c) Article 173
(d) Article 191

List-II
i. Disqualifications for membership of State Legislatures
ii. Qualifications for membership of Parliament
iii. Disqualifications for membership of Parliament
iv. Qualifications for membership of State Legislatures
mcqs.explanation: The RPA, 1951 is connected with Article 84 on qualifications for Parliament, Article 102 on parliamentary disqualifications, Article 173 on State Legislature qualifications, and Article 191 on State Legislature disqualifications.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Supreme Court upheld the removal of the particular-State elector requirement for Rajya Sabha candidates in Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India, 2006.
Statement B: The 2003 Amendment required a Rajya Sabha candidate to be an elector in the State from which the candidate contested.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true: the Supreme Court upheld the 2003 change in Kuldip Nayar (2006). Statement B is false because the 2003 Amendment removed, rather than imposed, the particular-State elector requirement.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968:
I. It is not issued by Parliament for recognizing political parties.
II. It is not issued by the Ministry of Law and Justice for recognizing political parties.
III. It is not issued by the President for recognizing political parties.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Recognition of political parties is under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968, and the Order is not issued by Parliament, the Ministry of Law and Justice, or the President.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the registration of political parties:
Statement A: The Ministry of Law and Justice is not the authority that registers political parties.
Statement B: Parliament is not the authority that registers political parties.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Political parties are registered by the Election Commission of India under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, not by the Ministry of Law and Justice or Parliament.

mcqs.question: Under the merger exception to disqualification on grounds of defection, what minimum proportion of the members of a legislative party must agree to the merger?
mcqs.explanation: The merger protection applies when at least two-thirds of the members of the legislative party agree to the merger.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Disqualification may arise when a member voluntarily gives up party membership.
Disqualification on defection does not apply when at least two-thirds of the legislative party members agree to a merger.
Disqualification on defection does not apply when one-third of the legislative party members agree to a merger.
Disqualification may arise when a member votes contrary to the party whip without prior permission.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the one-third threshold. Merger protection requires agreement by at least two-thirds of the legislative party members; the one-third split exemption was omitted by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The original one-third split exemption is no longer available under the anti-defection provisions.
Reason (R): The one-third split exemption was omitted by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the omission of the one-third split exemption by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 explains why it is no longer available.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Formation of CPI(M)
B. Formation of the Indian National Congress
C. Formation of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh
D. Formation of the Communist Party of India
mcqs.explanation: The sequence is INC (1885), CPI (1925), BJS (1951), and CPI(M) formation after the CPI split (1964).

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
 a. Indian National Congress
 b. Bharatiya Jana Sangh
 c. Bharatiya Janata Party
 d. Nationalist Congress Party

List-II
 i. First President: Atal Bihari Vajpayee
 ii. Founder: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee
 iii. First President: W.C. Banerjee
 iv. Split from INC by Sharad Pawar, P.A. Sangma and Tariq Anwar
