mcqs.explanation: The constitutional framework is governed under Part XI, Articles 245–255 and the Seventh Schedule. Article 246A was introduced as a special GST provision through the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.

mcqs.question: Under Article 246(1), which body has exclusive legislative competence over the Union List?
mcqs.explanation: Article 246(1) gives Parliament exclusive legislative competence over List I, the Union List.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. State Legislatures have exclusive legislative competence over the State List.
II. Both Parliament and State Legislatures have competence over the Concurrent List.
III. Parliament has exclusive competence over the Union List.
IV. State Legislatures have exclusive competence over the Concurrent List.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III correctly describe Article 246. Statement IV is incorrect because the Concurrent List is subject to legislative competence of both Parliament and State Legislatures.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Railways
(b) Police
(c) Education
(d) Marriage, Divorce and Adoption

List-II
(i) Union List
(ii) State List
(iii) Concurrent List
(iv) Subject shifted to the Concurrent List by the 42nd CAA
mcqs.explanation: Railways is in the Union List; Police is in the State List; Education was shifted to the Concurrent List by the 42nd CAA; and Marriage, Divorce and Adoption are in the Concurrent List.

mcqs.question: Under Article 248, residuary legislative powers are vested exclusively in:
options: Both Parliament and State Legislatures equally
mcqs.explanation: Article 248 vests exclusive legislative competence over subjects not enumerated in any of the three Lists in Parliament.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In case of conflict on a Concurrent List subject, the Central law generally prevails.
Repugnancy between Central and State laws on a Concurrent List subject is dealt with under Article 250.
The general rule of Central law prevailing is subject to the exception relating to Presidential assent.
A State law on a Concurrent List subject may prevail if it was reserved for Presidential assent and received such assent under Article 254(2).
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is Article 250. Repugnancy on a Concurrent List subject is governed by Article 254; Article 250 concerns legislation during a National Emergency.

mcqs.question:
Which of the following subjects were transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
I. Education
II. Forests
III. Weights and Measures
IV. Protection of Wild Animals and Birds
mcqs.explanation: All four listed subjects were among the five subjects transferred by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. The fifth was Administration of Justice, with the stated limitation concerning the Supreme Court and High Courts.

mcqs.question: Which subject was inserted as Entry 20A in the Concurrent List?
options: Protection of Wild Animals and Birds
mcqs.explanation: Entry 20A, dealing with Population Control and Family Planning, was inserted into the Concurrent List.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Article 249
(b) Article 250
(c) Article 252
(d) Article 253

List-II
(i) Implementation of international treaties or agreements
(ii) National Emergency
(iii) Request by two or more State Legislatures
(iv) Rajya Sabha resolution in national interest
mcqs.explanation: Article 249 is triggered by a Rajya Sabha resolution in national interest; Article 250 by a National Emergency; Article 252 by resolutions of at least two State Legislatures; and Article 253 by international treaties or agreements.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Parliament may legislate on a State List subject under Article 249.
Reason (R): The Rajya Sabha must pass a resolution in the national interest by at least a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Article 249 permits Parliament to legislate on the State List when the Rajya Sabha adopts the specified national-interest resolution. The law remains in force for one year and ceases six months after the resolution lapses.

mcqs.question: A law made by Parliament under Article 249 remains in force for what period after the Rajya Sabha resolution lapses?
mcqs.explanation: A law made under Article 249 ceases six months after the Rajya Sabha resolution lapses.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Under Article 250, Parliament may legislate on State List subjects during the operation of a National Emergency.
Statement B: Such a law ceases six months after the National Emergency ends.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Article 250 operates during a National Emergency under Article 352. A law made under it ceases six months after the Emergency ends.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding Article 252 is incorrect?
options: The law can be amended or repealed only by Parliament.
The law applies only to the States that consented to it.
The law automatically applies to every State in India.
It operates when two or more State Legislatures request Parliament through resolutions.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the scope of application. An Article 252 law applies only to the consenting States; it does not automatically apply to every State.

mcqs.question: Article 253 empowers Parliament to enact laws for implementing:
options: Only State List subjects during ordinary conditions
mcqs.explanation: Article 253 gives Parliament plenary power to enact laws for implementing international conventions, treaties or agreements.

mcqs.question: When a Proclamation of President's Rule is in operation in a State, which Article enables Parliament to exercise the legislative powers of that State Legislature?
mcqs.explanation: Under Article 356, during President's Rule in a State, Parliament exercises the legislative powers of that State Legislature.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are Concurrent List subjects?
1. Railway Police
2. Economic and Social Planning
3. Census
4. Price Control
mcqs.explanation: Economic and Social Planning and Price Control are Concurrent List subjects. Railway Police is in the State List, while Census is in the Union List. Therefore, the count is two.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Corporation Tax is a Union List subject, whereas Land Revenue is a State List subject.
Statement B: Economic and Social Planning is a Union List subject.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is correct: Corporation Tax is in the Union List and Land Revenue is in the State List. Statement B is incorrect because Economic and Social Planning is in the Concurrent List.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Article 246A gives both Parliament and State Legislatures powers to frame laws regarding GST.
Statement B: Panchayati Raj and Municipalities are enumerated in the Union List.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Article 246A gives simultaneous GST legislative powers to Parliament and State Legislatures. Panchayati Raj and Municipalities are placed in the State List under Entry 5, not the Union List.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Inter-State Trade and Commerce
(b) Public Health and Sanitation
(c) Criminal Law and Criminal Procedure
(d) Corporation Tax

List-II
(i) State List
(ii) Concurrent List
(iii) Union List, Entry 42
(iv) Union List

Options:
mcqs.explanation: Inter-State Trade and Commerce is in the Union List under Entry 42; Public Health and Sanitation is in the State List; Criminal Law and Criminal Procedure are in the Concurrent List; and Corporation Tax is in the Union List.

mcqs.question: The Seventh Schedule is read with which constitutional Part and range of Articles?
mcqs.explanation: The constitutional framework of the Seventh Schedule is governed by Part XI, covering Articles 245–255.

mcqs.question: Which Article provides the special constitutional provision for Goods and Services Tax?
mcqs.explanation: Article 246A provides the special GST provision, introduced through the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A State law on a Concurrent List subject may prevail over a Central law in certain circumstances.
Reason (R): The State law must have been reserved for the President's consideration and must have received Presidential assent under Article 254(2).
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Presidential reservation and assent under Article 254(2) explain the stated exception to the general repugnancy rule.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Defence and Armed Forces
(b) Public Order
(c) Education
(d) Corporation Tax

List-II
(i) Union List
(ii) State List
(iii) Concurrent List
(iv) Union List
mcqs.explanation: Defence and Armed Forces and Corporation Tax are Union List subjects; Public Order is a State List subject; Education is in the Concurrent List.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Atomic Energy and Mineral Resources are Union List subjects.
II. Public Health and Sanitation is a State List subject.
III. Local Government and Panchayati Raj are State List subjects.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and III are correct. Public Health and Sanitation is listed under the Concurrent List, making Statement II incorrect.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Radio and Television Broadcasting is a Union List subject.
Statement B: Electricity is a Concurrent List subject.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both Radio and Television Broadcasting and Electricity are included in the Union-plus-State Concurrent List in the comparison table.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Agriculture and Agricultural Education
(b) Stock Exchanges and Futures Markets
(c) Adulteration of Foodstuffs and Goods
(d) Tolls and Capitation Taxes

List-II
(i) State List
(ii) Union List
(iii) Concurrent List
(iv) State List
mcqs.explanation: Agriculture and Agricultural Education and Tolls and Capitation Taxes are State List subjects; Stock Exchanges and Futures Markets is Union List; Adulteration of Foodstuffs and Goods is Concurrent List.

mcqs.question: Trade and commerce within a State is placed in which List, subject to the relevant Concurrent List entry?
mcqs.explanation: Trade and Commerce within a State is a State List subject under Entry 26, subject to List III Entry 33.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the five subjects transferred by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
options: Public Order was transferred to the Concurrent List.
Administration of Justice was transferred to the Concurrent List.
Weights and Measures was transferred to the Concurrent List.
Protection of Wild Animals and Birds was transferred to the Concurrent List.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is Public Order. The five transferred subjects included Education, Forests, Weights and Measures, Protection of Wild Animals and Birds, and Administration of Justice.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Education
(b) Forests
(c) Weights and Measures
(d) Administration of Justice

List-II
(i) Subject transferred to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment
(ii) Subject transferred to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment
(iii) Subject transferred to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment
(iv) Subject transferred to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment
mcqs.explanation: All four listed subjects—Education, Forests, Weights and Measures, and Administration of Justice—were transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following were transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
1. Weights and Measures
2. Protection of Wild Animals and Birds
3. Administration of Justice
4. Public Health and Sanitation
mcqs.explanation: The first three were among the five transferred subjects. Public Health and Sanitation was not included in that five-subject transfer.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A law made by Parliament under Article 250 ceases to operate six months after the National Emergency ends.
Reason (R): Article 250 operates when a National Emergency under Article 352 is in force.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the Reason states the triggering condition and does not explain the six-month post-emergency limit.

mcqs.question:
Match the constitutional gateways with their triggering mechanisms:

List-I
(a) Article 249
(b) Article 250
(c) Article 252
(d) Article 356

List-II
(i) Request by two or more State Legislatures
(ii) National Emergency
(iii) Rajya Sabha resolution in national interest
(iv) Proclamation of President's Rule in a State
mcqs.explanation: Article 249 follows a Rajya Sabha national-interest resolution; Article 250 follows a National Emergency; Article 252 follows requests by State Legislatures; Article 356 follows President's Rule.

mcqs.question: Article 253 confers plenary power on Parliament to enact laws for implementing:
options: Only laws reserved by State Governors
State List resolutions passed by Municipalities
Only recommendations of the Finance Commission
mcqs.explanation: Article 253 enables Parliament to enact laws for implementing international treaties, agreements, conventions and accords.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: During a Proclamation of President's Rule in a State, Parliament exercises the legislative powers of that State Legislature.
Statement B: Article 356 is a gateway through which Parliament may legislate in place of the State Legislature.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements correctly describe the Article 356 gateway during a Proclamation of President's Rule.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are State List subjects?
1. Agriculture and Agricultural Education
2. Land and Land Reforms
3. Fisheries and Markets/Fairs
4. Radio and Television Broadcasting
mcqs.explanation: The first three are State List subjects. Radio and Television Broadcasting is a Union List subject.

mcqs.question: Which Article breaks the strict exclusive-list pattern by giving simultaneous legislative powers to Parliament and State Legislatures regarding GST?
mcqs.explanation: Article 246A gives both Parliament and State Legislatures simultaneous powers to frame laws regarding GST.

mcqs.question: Under Article 246(2), legislative competence over the Concurrent List is vested in:
options: The President and State Governors jointly
mcqs.explanation: Article 246(2) provides concurrent legislative competence to both Parliament and State Legislatures over the Concurrent List.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is included in the Concurrent List?
mcqs.explanation: The Civil Procedure Code (CPC) is listed under the Concurrent List. Foreign Affairs and Treaties, Census and Corporation Tax are Union List subjects.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Foreign Affairs and Treaties
(b) Tolls and Capitation Taxes
(c) Civil Procedure Code
(d) Prevention of Cruelty to Animals

List-II
(i) Union List
(ii) State List
(iii) Concurrent List
mcqs.explanation: Foreign Affairs and Treaties belong to the Union List; Tolls and Capitation Taxes to the State List; and the Civil Procedure Code and Prevention of Cruelty to Animals to the Concurrent List.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Local Government and Panchayati Raj are placed in the State List.
Statement B: Stock Exchanges and Futures Markets are placed in the Concurrent List.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Local Government and Panchayati Raj are State List subjects under Entry 5. Stock Exchanges and Futures Markets are Union List subjects, not Concurrent List subjects.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are Union List subjects?
1. Foreign Affairs and Treaties
2. Banking and Insurance
3. Stock Exchanges and Futures Markets
4. Inter-State Migration and Quarantine
mcqs.explanation: All four listed subjects—Foreign Affairs and Treaties, Banking and Insurance, Stock Exchanges and Futures Markets, and Inter-State Migration and Quarantine—are in the Union List.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the distribution of subjects?
options: Public Health and Sanitation is a Concurrent List subject.
Tolls and Capitation Taxes are State List subjects.
Inter-State Migration and Quarantine are Union List subjects.
Local Government and Panchayati Raj are State List subjects.
mcqs.explanation: Public Health and Sanitation is a State List subject, not a Concurrent List subject. The other three statements are correct.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A law enacted under Article 252 applies only to the States that consented to it.
Reason (R): Article 252 is activated by resolutions passed by at least two State Legislatures requesting Parliament to legislate.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Article 252 permits Parliament to legislate on a State List subject when at least two State Legislatures request it. The resulting law applies only to the consenting States.

mcqs.question: A law made by Parliament under Article 252 can be amended or repealed by:
mcqs.explanation: A law enacted under Article 252 can be amended or repealed only by Parliament.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Article 253 gives Parliament plenary power to enact laws for implementing international conventions and accords.
Reason (R): Article 253 is a gateway for implementing international treaties and agreements.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Article 253 empowers Parliament to enact laws for implementing international treaties, agreements, conventions and accords. This treaty-implementation function explains the assertion.

mcqs.question: Under Article 250, laws made by Parliament on State List subjects may extend to:
options: Only the State where the emergency originated
The whole or any part of India
mcqs.explanation: During a National Emergency, Article 250 permits Parliament to legislate on State List subjects for the whole or any part of India.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect about the five subjects transferred by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
options: Administration of Justice was transferred to the Concurrent List.
Forests were transferred to the Concurrent List.
Public Health and Sanitation was transferred to the Concurrent List.
Education was transferred to the Concurrent List.
mcqs.explanation: Public Health and Sanitation was not one of the five subjects transferred by the 42nd Amendment. Education, Forests and Administration of Justice were among the subjects shifted to the Concurrent List.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Education
(b) Forests
(c) Weights and Measures
(d) Protection of Wild Animals and Birds

List-II
(i) Subject transferred to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment
(ii) Subject remaining in the State List

Choose the correct code.
mcqs.explanation: All four subjects listed—Education, Forests, Weights and Measures, and Protection of Wild Animals and Birds—were transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Administration of Justice was one of the subjects transferred to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment.
II. The transfer covered the constitution and organisation of all courts except the Supreme Court and High Courts.
III. Population Control and Family Planning was inserted as Entry 20A in the Concurrent List.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Administration of Justice was transferred with the stated exception for the Supreme Court and High Courts, and Entry 20A on Population Control and Family Planning was inserted in the Concurrent List.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Article 356 enables Parliament to exercise the legislative powers of the State Legislature during President's Rule in that State.
Statement B: Article 250 is activated by a request from at least two State Legislatures.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Article 356 enables Parliament to exercise the legislative powers of the State Legislature during President's Rule. Article 250 operates during a National Emergency, not on the request of State Legislatures.

mcqs.question: Panchayati Raj and Municipalities are enumerated in which List under Entry 5?
options: Residuary subjects outside the three Lists
mcqs.explanation: Local Self-Government, including Panchayati Raj and Municipalities, is placed in the State List under Entry 5.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Tolls and Capitation Taxes are State List subjects.
II. Fisheries and Markets or Fairs are State List subjects.
III. Prevention of Cruelty to Animals is a Union List subject.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Tolls and Capitation Taxes and Fisheries and Markets or Fairs are State List subjects. Prevention of Cruelty to Animals is in the Concurrent List, so Statement III is incorrect.

mcqs.question: Under Article 249, a Rajya Sabha resolution authorising Parliament to legislate on a State List subject in the national interest must be passed by:
options: The unanimous vote of all Rajya Sabha members
A majority of members present and voting
At least two-thirds of the total membership of the Rajya Sabha
At least two-thirds of members present and voting
mcqs.explanation: Article 249 requires a Rajya Sabha resolution in the national interest to be passed by at least two-thirds of the members present and voting.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Space research
(b) Cyber law
(c) Prisons
(d) Reformatories

List-II
(i) Residuary subject
(ii) State List subject
mcqs.explanation: Space research and cyber law are examples of residuary subjects. Prisons and reformatories are State List subjects.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Decennial enumerations are covered under the Union List subject of census.
Statement B: Land assessment is a State List subject.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Census, including decennial enumerations, is a Union List subject. Land assessment belongs to the State List.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Residuary powers lie with the States in the United States of America and Australia.
Reason (R): Residuary powers lie with the Centre in Canada.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: The assertion and reason are both true comparative positions. However, Canada's allocation of residuary powers to the Centre does not explain why they lie with the States in the United States of America and Australia.

mcqs.question: The Supreme Court of India is governed under which Part, Chapter and range of Articles of the Constitution?
mcqs.explanation: The Supreme Court is governed under Part V, Chapter IV, covering Articles 124–147.

mcqs.question: The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on:
mcqs.explanation: The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on 28 January 1950.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Supreme Court succeeded the Federal Court of India.
The Supreme Court succeeded the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council.
The Supreme Court succeeded the Council of States established under the Government of India Act, 1935.
The Federal Court was established under the Government of India Act, 1935.
mcqs.explanation: The altered detail is the alleged predecessor. The Supreme Court succeeded the Federal Court of India and the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council.

mcqs.question: The power to increase the number of Supreme Court judges is vested exclusively in:
options: The Supreme Court through its rules
mcqs.explanation: The power to increase the number of Supreme Court judges is vested exclusively in Parliament by law under Article 124(1).

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: A Supreme Court judge retires at the age of 65 years.
Statement B: A Supreme Court judge may be removed by the President following an Address supported by a Special Majority in each House of Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. Retirement is governed by Article 124(2), while removal is governed by Article 124(4).

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Original and exclusive jurisdiction
(b) Writ jurisdiction
(c) Review jurisdiction
(d) Advisory jurisdiction

List-II
(i) Article 137
(ii) Article 143
(iii) Article 131
(iv) Article 32
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-iii, b-iv, c-i and d-ii: Articles 131, 32, 137 and 143 respectively.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 131 is incorrect?
options: It includes recovery of damages by a private party against the Union.
It excludes inter-State water disputes under Article 262.
It covers disputes between one State and another State.
It covers direct federal disputes involving a legal right between the Centre and one or more States.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the inclusion of private-party recovery of damages. Recovery of damages by a private party against the Union is not covered under Article 131.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court cannot refuse an Article 32 petition.
Reason (R): Article 32 itself is a Fundamental Right.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the status of Article 32 as a Fundamental Right explains why the Supreme Court cannot refuse such a petition.

mcqs.question: Which of the following writs is included in the Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction under Article 32?
mcqs.explanation: Under Article 32, the Supreme Court issues Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction under Article 32 directly enforces Fundamental Rights.
Statement B: The Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction is broader than that of the High Courts under Article 226.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true because Article 32 concerns direct enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Statement B is false because Article 226 covers Fundamental Rights as well as legal rights and is therefore wider in scope.

mcqs.question:
Match the appellate jurisdiction with its governing Article:

List-I
(a) Constitutional appeals
(b) Civil appeals
(c) Criminal appeals
(d) Special Leave Petition

List-II
(i) Article 136
(ii) Article 134
(iii) Article 132
(iv) Article 133
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are constitutional appeals–Article 132, civil appeals–Article 133, criminal appeals–Article 134 and SLP–Article 136.

mcqs.question: Under Article 136, the Supreme Court's power to grant Special Leave to Appeal is:
options: Discretionary and available against any judgment or order of any court or tribunal, subject to the stated exception
Mandatory and limited to High Court judgments
Advisory and limited to presidential references
Available only in civil proceedings involving a constitutional question
mcqs.explanation: Article 136 confers a discretionary appellate power to grant leave against any judgment or order of any court or tribunal, excluding military tribunals and Armed Forces Courts under Article 136(2).

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court's review jurisdiction under Article 137 is distinct from judicial review of statutes.
Reason (R): Article 137 concerns the power of the Supreme Court to review its own judgments or orders.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 137 concerns review of the Supreme Court's own judgments or orders, making it distinct from judicial review of statutes.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): An opinion rendered by the Supreme Court to the President under Article 143 is not binding on the President.
Reason (R): Article 143 provides the Supreme Court with advisory jurisdiction.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the advisory character of Article 143 does not by itself fully explain the specific statement about binding status; the notes expressly state that such opinions are not binding on the President.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Under Article 143(1), the President may refer questions of law or fact of public importance to the Supreme Court.
II. Under Article 143(1), the Supreme Court may tender its opinion.
III. Under Article 143(2), the Supreme Court must tender its opinion on pre-constitutional matters.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Article 143(1) concerns public importance and permits the Court to tender an opinion, while Article 143(2) requires an opinion on pre-constitutional matters.

mcqs.question: What does Article 141 provide?
options: The Supreme Court may punish for contempt of Parliament.
The President may refer questions of public importance to the Supreme Court.
The law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within the territory of India.
The Supreme Court may review its own judgments.
mcqs.explanation: Article 141 provides that the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within the territory of India.

mcqs.question: Article 142 empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for:
options: Reviewing every statute enacted by Parliament
Doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it
mcqs.explanation: Article 142 empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.

mcqs.question:
Match the item with the corresponding detail:

List-I
(a) Curative Petition
(b) Constitution Bench
(c) Supreme Court as Court of Record
(d) Supreme Court Collegium

List-II
(i) Article 129
(ii) Article 145(3)
(iii) Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra, 2002
(iv) CJI plus four senior-most Supreme Court judges
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are curative petition–Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra, 2002; Constitution Bench–Article 145(3); Court of Record–Article 129; Collegium–CJI plus four senior-most judges.

mcqs.question: What is the minimum number of judges required for a Constitution Bench to hear a case involving a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution?
mcqs.explanation: Article 145(3) requires a minimum of five judges for such a Constitution Bench, and also for references under Article 143.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the Three Judges Cases in chronological order:
A. Third Judges Case
B. First Judges Case
C. Second Judges Case
D. Supreme Court Collegium framework evolved through these cases
mcqs.explanation: The First, Second and Third Judges Cases occurred in 1981, 1993 and 1998 respectively; the collegium framework evolved through these cases.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The collegium consists of the CJI and four senior-most Supreme Court judges.
II. The collegium has five members in total.
III. The collegium was created by an Act of Parliament.
IV. The collegium is explicitly written in the Constitution.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. The collegium was judicially evolved through the Three Judges Cases and was neither created by an Act of Parliament nor explicitly written in the Constitution.

mcqs.question: The Supreme Court of India succeeded which of the following institutions?
options: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council and the Constituent Assembly
The Federal Court of India and the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council
The Federal Court of India and the Finance Commission
The High Court of Calcutta and the Federal Court of India
mcqs.explanation: The Supreme Court succeeded both the Federal Court of India, established under the Government of India Act, 1935, and the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the removal of a Supreme Court judge is incorrect?
options: The judge may be removed by the President on the recommendation of the Chief Justice of India alone.
Removal may be made on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
The judge is removed by the President.
Removal requires an Address supported by a Special Majority in each House of Parliament.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that the Chief Justice of India alone can recommend removal. Removal requires a Parliamentary Address supported by a Special Majority in each House, followed by action by the President.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Special Leave Petition jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is not available against judgments or sentences passed by military tribunals.
Reason (R): Article 136(2) excludes courts-martial and military tribunals from the Special Leave Petition jurisdiction.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 136(2) specifically excludes courts-martial and military tribunals from the Supreme Court's Special Leave Petition jurisdiction.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction under Article 32 is narrower than that of the High Courts under Article 226.
Statement B: Article 226 enables High Courts to deal with Fundamental Rights as well as legal rights.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 32 concerns direct enforcement of Fundamental Rights, whereas Article 226 covers Fundamental Rights and legal rights.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. A constitutional appeal under Article 132 concerns a substantial question of law relating to the interpretation of the Constitution.
II. A civil appeal under Article 133 concerns a substantial question of law of general importance.
III. A criminal appeal under Article 134 may arise where a High Court reverses an acquittal and sentences the accused to death.
IV. Every criminal appeal under Article 134 requires a certificate from the High Court.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. Statement IV is incorrect because an appeal is available as of right in capital-punishment reversals without a High Court certificate.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Article 131
(b) Article 136
(c) Article 137
(d) Article 143

List-II
(i) Review jurisdiction
(ii) Advisory jurisdiction
(iii) Original and exclusive jurisdiction
(iv) Special Leave Petition jurisdiction
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Article 131–Original and exclusive jurisdiction, Article 136–SLP jurisdiction, Article 137–Review jurisdiction, and Article 143–Advisory jurisdiction.

mcqs.question: Under Article 143(2), the Supreme Court is required to tender its opinion on which category of matters?
options: Private claims for damages against the Union
mcqs.explanation: Under Article 143(2), the Supreme Court must tender its opinion on pre-constitutional matters.

mcqs.question: The curative petition was evolved by the Supreme Court in which case and year?
options: Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra, 2002
Ashok Hurra v. Rupa Ashok Hurra, 2002
Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra, 1998
Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra, 1993
mcqs.explanation: The curative petition was evolved in Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra in 2002.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Article 142 gives the Supreme Court a power that can operate unhindered by ordinary statutory limitations.
Reason (R): Article 142 empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in a cause or matter pending before it.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The power to do complete justice under Article 142 explains why the provision operates unhindered by ordinary statutory limitations.

mcqs.question: Which Article recognises the Supreme Court as a Court of Record?
mcqs.explanation: Article 129 recognises the Supreme Court as a Court of Record and gives it inherent power to punish for contempt of itself.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Supreme Court's decisions as a Court of Record have evidentiary value and cannot be questioned in subordinate courts.
Statement B: Article 215 provides parallel Court of Record status to High Courts at the State level.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 129 applies to the Supreme Court, while Article 215 provides Court of Record status to High Courts at the State level.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Article 129
(b) Article 142
(c) Article 145(3)
(d) Article 215

List-II
(i) High Court as Court of Record
(ii) Constitution Bench
(iii) Supreme Court as Court of Record
(iv) Complete Justice
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Article 129–Supreme Court as Court of Record, Article 142–Complete Justice, Article 145(3)–Constitution Bench, and Article 215–High Court as Court of Record.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the constitutional status of the Supreme Court Collegium?
options: It is explicitly written in the Constitution.
It is expressly created by an Act of Parliament.
It is created under Article 143 by the President.
It was judicially evolved and is neither created by an Act of Parliament nor explicitly written in the Constitution.
mcqs.explanation: The Collegium framework was judicially evolved through the Three Judges Cases. It is neither created by an Act of Parliament nor explicitly written in the Constitution.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following matters are excluded from the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction under Article 131?
I. Inter-State water disputes
II. Finance Commission matters
III. Recovery of damages by a private party against the Union
IV. Direct federal disputes involving a legal right between States
mcqs.explanation: The first three matters are excluded from Article 131 jurisdiction. Direct federal disputes involving a legal right between States fall within its core scope.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding Special Leave Petition jurisdiction is incorrect?
options: It may be exercised against a judgment or order of any court or tribunal, subject to the constitutional exclusion.
It is a discretionary appellate power of the Supreme Court.
It is an appeal available as of right in every case before any court or tribunal.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that SLP is available as of right. Article 136 confers a discretionary, plenary and residual appellate power.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: A constitutional appeal under Article 132 requires a certificate from the High Court under Article 134A.
Statement B: A civil appeal under Article 133 requires the High Court to certify under Article 134A that the substantial question of law needs determination by the Supreme Court.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 134A provides the relevant High Court certification mechanism for constitutional and civil appeals.

mcqs.question: Which situation specifically attracts an appeal under Article 134 of the Constitution?
options: A High Court decides a private claim for damages against the Union.
A High Court reverses an acquittal and sentences the accused to death.
A High Court refers a pre-constitutional matter to the President.
A High Court hears an inter-State water dispute.
mcqs.explanation: Article 134 covers criminal appeals, including cases where a High Court reverses an acquittal and sentences the accused to death.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. A Constitution Bench requires a minimum of five judges.
II. It may hear a case involving a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution.
III. It may hear references under Article 143.
IV. A Constitution Bench must consist of exactly seven judges.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. The notes prescribe a minimum of five judges, not an exact requirement of seven judges.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A curative petition may be pursued after dismissal of a review petition under Article 137.
Reason (R): The curative petition was evolved under the Supreme Court's inherent powers anchored in Article 142 to prevent abuse of process and cure gross miscarriages of justice.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The curative petition follows dismissal of a review petition and rests on the inherent powers associated with Article 142.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Political questions without legal rights
(b) Pre-Constitution treaties or agreements
(c) Inter-State water disputes
(d) Finance Commission matters

List-II
(i) Excluded under Article 262
(ii) Excluded from Article 131
(iii) Excluded under the Article 131 proviso
(iv) Not covered by Article 131 because Article 280 is relevant
mcqs.explanation: Political questions without legal rights are excluded from Article 131; pre-Constitution treaties are excluded by its proviso; inter-State water disputes fall under Article 262; and Finance Commission matters relate to Article 280.

mcqs.question: An appeal under Article 133 of the Constitution lies from a High Court judgment in a civil proceeding involving:
options: A substantial question of law relating to the interpretation of the Constitution
A criminal proceeding in which the High Court has reversed an acquittal
Any question of fact referred by the President
A substantial question of law of general importance requiring determination by the Supreme Court
mcqs.explanation: Article 133 covers appeals in civil proceedings involving a substantial question of law of general importance. The High Court must certify that the question needs determination by the Supreme Court.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding civil appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is incorrect?
options: It concerns appeals in civil proceedings.
It concerns only a substantial question of law relating to the interpretation of the Constitution.
The substantial question of law must be of general importance.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement alters the subject matter. Article 133 concerns a substantial question of law of general importance, whereas interpretation of the Constitution is covered under Article 132.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Article 133 deals with appeals in civil proceedings.
Statement B: Article 136 gives an automatic right of appeal in every civil proceeding.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true because Article 133 concerns civil appeals. Statement B is false because Article 136 confers a discretionary power to grant special leave, not an automatic right of appeal.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Article 133
(b) Article 134
(c) Article 137
(d) Article 143

List-II
(i) Review of the Supreme Court's own judgments or orders
(ii) Appeals in specified criminal proceedings
(iii) Appeals in civil proceedings involving a substantial question of law of general importance
(iv) Opinion on questions referred by the President
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Article 133—civil appeals, Article 134—specified criminal appeals, Article 137—review jurisdiction, and Article 143—advisory jurisdiction.

mcqs.question: Apart from the evidentiary value of its decisions, the Supreme Court as a Court of Record has the inherent power to:
options: Refer every constitutional question to the President
Certify every civil appeal to the High Court
Increase the number of its judges
mcqs.explanation: Under Article 129, the Supreme Court is a Court of Record and has the inherent power to punish for contempt of itself.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court and the High Courts both possess Court of Record status.
Reason (R): Article 129 relates to the Supreme Court, while Article 215 relates to the High Courts.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 129 establishes the Supreme Court as a Court of Record, and Article 215 provides parallel Court of Record status to the High Courts at the State level.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding a Constitution Bench:
I. It requires a minimum of five judges.
II. It may hear a case involving a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution.
III. It may hear references under Article 143.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Article 145(3) requires a minimum of five judges for constitutional-interpretation cases and references under Article 143.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following Articles are expressly associated with a power or function of the Supreme Court mentioned below?
1. Article 141 — binding precedent
2. Article 142 — complete justice
3. Article 143 — advisory jurisdiction
4. Article 145(3) — Constitution Bench
mcqs.explanation: All four entries are correctly associated: Articles 141, 142 and 143 concern binding precedent, complete justice and advisory jurisdiction respectively, while Article 145(3) concerns Constitution Benches.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the two clauses of Article 143 is incorrect?
options: Under Article 143(1), the President may refer a question of law or fact of public importance.
Under Article 143(2), the Supreme Court may decline to tender its opinion.
Under Article 143(1), the Supreme Court may tender its opinion.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement alters the obligation under Article 143(2). For pre-constitutional matters, the Supreme Court must tender its opinion; the discretionary wording applies to Article 143(1).

mcqs.question:
Match the constitutional provision with the corresponding subject:

List-I
(a) Article 124(1)
(b) Article 124(2)
(c) Article 124(4)
(d) Article 134A

List-II
(i) Certificate for appeal to the Supreme Court
(ii) Retirement age of Supreme Court judges
(iii) Removal of a Supreme Court judge
(iv) Parliament's power to increase the number of Supreme Court judges
mcqs.explanation: Article 124(1) concerns the number of judges, Article 124(2) concerns retirement, Article 124(4) concerns removal, and Article 134A concerns certification for appeals.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following appellate jurisdictions expressly require certification by the High Court under Article 134A?
1. Constitutional appeals under Article 132
2. Civil appeals under Article 133
3. Criminal appeals under Article 134
4. Special Leave Petition jurisdiction under Article 136
mcqs.explanation: Two listed jurisdictions—constitutional appeals under Article 132 and civil appeals under Article 133—require a High Court certificate under Article 134A. The notes describe criminal appeals in the specified cases as available as of right and Article 136 as discretionary.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court Collegium:
I. Its composition is the Chief Justice of India and four senior-most Supreme Court judges.
II. It has a total of five members.
III. It was created by an Act of Parliament.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. The Collegium consists of the CJI and four senior-most Supreme Court judges, but it was judicially evolved and was neither created by an Act of Parliament nor explicitly written in the Constitution.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32:
I. The Supreme Court can issue the writ of Mandamus.
II. The Supreme Court can issue the writ of Prohibition.
III. The Supreme Court can issue the writ of Certiorari.
IV. The Supreme Court can issue the writ of Quo Warranto.
mcqs.explanation: Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto. Therefore, all four statements are correct.

mcqs.question: Which of the following disputes falls within the Supreme Court’s original and exclusive jurisdiction under Article 131?
options: A dispute arising from a pre-Constitution treaty or agreement
A dispute involving only political questions without legal rights
A dispute between the Centre and one or more States on one side and other States on the other side
mcqs.explanation: Article 131 covers direct federal disputes involving a legal right, including disputes where the Centre and one or more States are on one side and other States are on the other side. Political questions without legal rights, pre-Constitution treaties or agreements, and inter-State water disputes are excluded.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court’s review jurisdiction under Article 137 is subject to Parliamentary law and court rules.
Reason (R): Article 137 empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgments or orders.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 137 concerns the Supreme Court’s power to review its own judgments or orders, while the exercise of this review jurisdiction is subject to Parliamentary law and court rules; the Reason does not explain that limitation.

70.title: High Courts: Articles, Powers and Jurisdiction

mcqs.question: The constitutional provisions relating to High Courts are contained in which Part, Chapter and range of Articles?
mcqs.explanation: High Courts are governed under Part VI, Chapter V, covering Articles 214–231.

mcqs.question: Which was among the first three High Courts established in 1862 under the Indian High Courts Act, 1861?
mcqs.explanation: The first three High Courts were established at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras in 1862.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. High Court for North-Western Provinces established at Agra
B. Agra High Court shifted to Allahabad
C. First three High Courts established at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras
mcqs.explanation: The first three High Courts were established in 1862, the Agra High Court in 1866, and it was shifted to Allahabad in 1869.

mcqs.question: Under Article 216, who decides and fixes the strength or number of judges of a High Court?
options: The Chief Minister of the State
mcqs.explanation: Article 216 provides that the strength of a High Court is decided and fixed by the President of India.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Article 215
(b) Article 216
(c) Article 222
(d) Article 231

List-II
(i) Transfer of a Judge from one High Court to another
(ii) Common High Court for two or more States or Union Territories
(iii) High Courts as Courts of Record
(iv) Composition of High Courts
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Article 215–Court of Record, 216–Composition, 222–Transfer, and 231–Common High Court.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: High Court judges are appointed by the President of India by warrant.
Statement B: The oath of a High Court judge is administered by the President of India.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: High Court judges are appointed by the President by warrant, while their oath is administered by the Governor of the State.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A High Court judge submits resignation to the President of India.
Reason (R): The oath of office of a High Court judge is administered by the Governor of the State.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the Governor administering the oath does not explain why resignation is addressed to the President.

mcqs.question:
Match the constitutional parameters with the corresponding High Court provisions:
List-I
(a) Retirement age
(b) Oath administered by
(c) Resignation addressed to
(d) Court of Record

List-II
(i) President of India
(ii) 62 years
(iii) Governor of the State
(iv) Article 215
mcqs.explanation: A High Court judge retires at 62, takes oath before the Governor, resigns to the President, and the Court of Record provision is Article 215.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The salary of a High Court judge is charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
The salary and pension of a High Court judge are both charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
The High Court judge’s retirement age is 62 years.
The pension of a High Court judge is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement changes the pension source. Salary is charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State, whereas pension is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Article 220 deals with restriction on practice after being a permanent High Court judge.
II. Article 223 deals with appointment of an Acting Chief Justice.
III. Article 227 deals with the power of High Courts to issue certain writs.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. Article 227 concerns the High Court’s power of superintendence; writ power is dealt with under Article 226.

mcqs.question: The Chief Justice of a High Court is appointed by the President after consultation with which combination?
options: The Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the State
The Governor and the Chief Justice of that High Court
The Governor and the Chief Minister of the State
The Chief Justice of India and the Chief Justice of that High Court
mcqs.explanation: For appointment of a High Court Chief Justice, the President consults the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the State.

mcqs.question:
Which of the following are qualifications for appointment as a High Court judge?
I. The person must be a citizen of India.
II. The person must have held a judicial office in India for at least 10 years.
III. The person must have practised as an advocate of a High Court for at least 10 years.
IV. The person must be a distinguished jurist.
mcqs.explanation: A High Court judge must be an Indian citizen and satisfy either the 10-year judicial-office or 10-year High Court advocacy condition. There is no provision for appointing a distinguished jurist as a High Court judge.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding removal of a High Court judge is incorrect?
options: The judge may be removed by the Governor after consultation with the Chief Justice of India.
The removal follows an address passed by each House of Parliament by Special Majority.
The judge can be removed only by the President.
Removal may be on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement changes the removing authority. A High Court judge is removed by the President after the required Special Majority address by each House of Parliament.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Article 218
(b) Article 224/224A
(c) Article 226
(d) Article 230

List-II
(i) Extension of jurisdiction to Union Territories
(ii) Application of certain Supreme Court removal provisions
(iii) Writ jurisdiction
(iv) Additional or Acting Judges and attendance of retired Judges
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Article 218–removal provisions, 224/224A–Additional or Acting Judges and retired Judges, 226–writs, and 230–Union Territories.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The writ jurisdiction of a High Court is broader than that of the Supreme Court.
Reason (R): A High Court may issue writs for Fundamental Rights as well as for any other legal purpose or right.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the wider scope of Article 226—Fundamental Rights plus other legal rights or purposes—explains the assertion.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the High Court’s power of superintendence?
options: It extends to courts and tribunals constituted under laws relating to the Armed Forces.
It extends throughout the High Court’s territorial jurisdiction.
It includes administrative and judicial superintendence over subordinate courts and tribunals.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement reverses the Armed Forces exception. Article 227 superintendence does not extend to courts and tribunals constituted under laws relating to the Armed Forces.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Parliament may establish a Common High Court for two or more States and Union Territories under Article 231.
Statement B: Article 230 concerns the extension of High Court jurisdiction to Union Territories.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct: Article 231 concerns Common High Courts, while Article 230 concerns extension of jurisdiction to Union Territories.

mcqs.question:
Match the High Courts with the corresponding territories:
List-I
(a) Bombay High Court
(b) Calcutta High Court
(c) Kerala High Court
(d) Madras High Court

List-II
(i) Kerala and Lakshadweep
(ii) Tamil Nadu and Puducherry
(iii) Maharashtra, Goa, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
(iv) West Bengal and Andaman & Nicobar Islands
mcqs.explanation: The correct territorial pairs are Bombay–Maharashtra, Goa, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu; Calcutta–West Bengal and Andaman & Nicobar; Kerala–Lakshadweep; and Madras–Puducherry.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following territorial pairings are correct?
I. Punjab and Haryana High Court — Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh
II. Gauhati High Court — Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh
III. Kerala High Court — Kerala and Puducherry
IV. Madras High Court — Tamil Nadu and Lakshadweep
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. Kerala High Court covers Lakshadweep, while Madras High Court covers Puducherry.

mcqs.question: A retired permanent High Court judge cannot plead or act before any court or authority in India, except before which of the following?
options: The Supreme Court and other High Courts where the judge did not serve as a permanent judge
Only the High Court where the judge served permanently
The Supreme Court and all subordinate courts
mcqs.explanation: A retired permanent High Court judge may plead or act before the Supreme Court and other High Courts where the judge did not serve as a permanent judge.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect in comparing the High Court and the Supreme Court?
options: The High Court is a Court of Record under Article 215.
The High Court has general advisory jurisdiction under Article 143.
The Supreme Court is a Court of Record under Article 129.
The Supreme Court has advisory jurisdiction under Article 143.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement changes the jurisdiction of the High Court. The High Court has no general advisory jurisdiction, whereas the Supreme Court has advisory jurisdiction under Article 143.

mcqs.question: Which Article mandates a High Court for each State?
mcqs.explanation: Article 214 mandates a High Court for each State.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a consequence of a High Court being a Court of Record under Article 215?
options: It can exercise general advisory jurisdiction
It can appoint all subordinate court judges
It has evidentiary value and the power to punish for contempt
mcqs.explanation: Article 215 makes High Courts Courts of Record, giving their records evidentiary value and empowering them to punish for contempt.

mcqs.question: Which Article deals with the salaries, allowances and pensions of High Court judges?
mcqs.explanation: Article 221 deals with the salaries, allowances and pensions of High Court judges.

mcqs.question: Under which Article is an Acting Chief Justice of a High Court appointed?
mcqs.explanation: Article 223 provides for the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice of a High Court.

mcqs.question: Which constitutional provision relates to the appointment of Additional Judges, Acting Judges and the attendance of retired Judges of a High Court?
mcqs.explanation: Articles 224 and 224A concern Additional or Acting Judges and the attendance of retired Judges, respectively.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the financial provisions relating to High Court judges?
options: The salary of a High Court judge is charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
Salary and pension of High Court judges are both charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
The salary and pension are dealt with under the financial comparison of High Courts and the Supreme Court.
The pension of a High Court judge is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the source of pension. Salary is charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State, whereas pension is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Other High Court judges are appointed by the President after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the State and the Chief Justice of that High Court.
Reason (R): The consultation matrix for other High Court judges is wider than that prescribed for appointing the Chief Justice of a High Court.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The appointment of other High Court judges requires consultation with three constitutional authorities, whereas appointment of the Chief Justice involves the CJI and the State Governor.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Constitution does not provide for appointing a distinguished jurist as a High Court judge.
Reason (R): The provision for a distinguished jurist is mentioned in the qualifications for a Supreme Court judge, but not in those for a High Court judge.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both A and R are true, and the reason explains the distinction stated in the sheet: unlike the Supreme Court qualification provision, Article 217 does not include a distinguished jurist route.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The writ power of a High Court under Article 226 is discretionary.
Reason (R): Article 32 itself is a Fundamental Right.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the discretionary nature of Article 226. The notes distinguish the discretionary High Court writ power from Article 32, which itself is a Fundamental Right.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Article 215
(b) Article 221
(c) Article 223
(d) Article 227

List-II
(i) Appointment of Acting Chief Justice
(ii) Court of Record
(iii) Superintendence over courts and tribunals
(iv) Salaries, allowances and pensions
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-iv, c-i and d-iii.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Chief Justice of a High Court
(b) Other High Court judges
(c) High Court judge qualification
(d) Distinguished jurist

List-II
(i) No provision in the High Court qualification rule
(ii) President consults CJI and Governor
(iii) Citizen of India with the prescribed judicial office or advocacy experience
(iv) President consults CJI, Governor and Chief Justice of that High Court
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Chief Justice—consultation with CJI and Governor; other judges—consultation with CJI, Governor and Chief Justice of the High Court; qualification—citizenship plus the prescribed experience; distinguished jurist—no High Court provision.

mcqs.question:
Match the provision with its subject:

List-I
(a) Article 224
(b) Article 224A
(c) Article 227
(d) Article 230

List-II
(i) Attendance of retired Judges
(ii) Extension of jurisdiction to Union Territories
(iii) Additional and Acting Judges
(iv) Superintendence over subordinate courts and tribunals
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Article 224—Additional and Acting Judges, Article 224A—attendance of retired Judges, Article 227—superintendence, and Article 230—extension to Union Territories.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. A High Court is a Court of Record under Article 215.
II. A High Court's status as a Court of Record includes the power to punish for contempt.
III. Article 215 deals with the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. Article 223, not Article 215, deals with the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Article 227 concerns administrative superintendence by a High Court.
II. Article 227 concerns judicial superintendence by a High Court.
III. The power extends throughout the High Court's territorial jurisdiction.
IV. The power extends to courts constituted under laws relating to the Armed Forces.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. Statement IV is incorrect because courts and tribunals constituted under laws relating to the Armed Forces are excluded.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Salaries and allowances of High Court judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
Statement B: Pensions of High Court judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The notes distinguish the State source for salary and allowances from the Union Consolidated Fund source for pensions.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: A High Court has no general advisory jurisdiction.
Statement B: The Supreme Court has advisory jurisdiction under Article 143.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The High Court has no general advisory power, while the Supreme Court's advisory jurisdiction is under Article 143.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are features of the High Court's power of superintendence under Article 227?

I. Administrative superintendence
II. Judicial superintendence
III. Operation throughout its territorial jurisdiction
IV. Superintendence over Armed Forces courts constituted under a special law
mcqs.explanation: Only three statements are correct: I, II and III. Armed Forces courts and tribunals are excluded from the High Court's superintendence.

mcqs.question: Under which Article may a High Court issue writs for Fundamental Rights as well as for other legal purposes or rights?
mcqs.explanation: Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for Fundamental Rights and for any other legal purpose or right.

mcqs.question: The High Court for the North-Western Provinces was established at Agra in which year?
mcqs.explanation: The High Court for the North-Western Provinces was established at Agra in 1866. It was shifted to Allahabad in 1869.

mcqs.keyword: High Court vs Supreme Court – Strength
mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The strength of a High Court is decided by the President of India, whereas the strength of the Supreme Court is determined by Parliament by law.
Reason (R): Article 216 relates to the composition of High Courts, while Article 124(1) relates to the establishment and composition of the Supreme Court.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 216 provides for the composition of High Courts, with strength fixed by the President, while Article 124(1) provides for Parliament to determine the strength of the Supreme Court by law.

mcqs.keyword: High Court vs Supreme Court – Retirement Age
mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the retirement age of judges.

List-I
(a) Judge of a High Court
(b) Judge of the Supreme Court

List-II
(i) 62 years
(ii) 65 years
mcqs.explanation: A High Court judge retires at 62 years, while a Supreme Court judge retires at 65 years.

mcqs.question: Which Article declares the Supreme Court to be a Court of Record, corresponding to Article 215 for High Courts?
mcqs.explanation: Article 129 declares the Supreme Court to be a Court of Record. Article 215 contains the corresponding provision for High Courts.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Supreme Court has advisory jurisdiction under Article 143.
Statement B: A High Court has general advisory jurisdiction comparable to that of the Supreme Court.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The Supreme Court has advisory jurisdiction under Article 143. High Courts have no general advisory powers.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Article 226 permits High Courts to issue writs for Fundamental Rights.
II. Article 226 also permits High Courts to issue writs for other legal purposes or rights.
III. Article 32 of the Constitution gives the Supreme Court writ jurisdiction only in relation to Fundamental Rights.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. High Court writ jurisdiction under Article 226 extends to Fundamental Rights and other legal rights, whereas Article 32 concerns Fundamental Rights only.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the High Court's power of superintendence under Article 227?
options: It extends to courts and tribunals constituted under every law relating to the Armed Forces.
It includes judicial superintendence over subordinate courts and tribunals.
It includes administrative superintendence over subordinate courts and tribunals.
It operates throughout the territorial jurisdiction of the High Court.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that Article 227 extends to every Armed Forces court or tribunal. Article 227(4) excludes courts and tribunals constituted under laws relating to the Armed Forces.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Supreme Court appointment by warrant
(b) Supreme Court resignation addressed to
(c) Supreme Court writ jurisdiction
(d) Supreme Court advisory jurisdiction

List-II
(i) Article 32
(ii) President of India
(iii) Article 143
(iv) Article 124
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: appointment by warrant—Article 124; resignation addressed to the President; writ jurisdiction—Article 32; advisory jurisdiction—Article 143.

mcqs.keyword: High Court vs Supreme Court – Constitutional Parameters
mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements correctly describe the Supreme Court?

I. Its judges retire at 65 years.
II. Its writ jurisdiction is under Article 32.
III. It has advisory jurisdiction under Article 143.
IV. Its Court of Record provision is Article 215.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. Article 215 concerns High Courts as Courts of Record; the corresponding Supreme Court provision is Article 129.

mcqs.question: Why is the writ jurisdiction of a High Court considered broader than that of the Supreme Court?
options: Because a High Court can appoint Supreme Court judges
Because a High Court can issue writs only for Fundamental Rights
Because a High Court has general advisory jurisdiction
Because a High Court can issue writs for Fundamental Rights and other legal purposes or rights
mcqs.explanation: Article 226 enables a High Court to issue writs for Fundamental Rights as well as for other legal purposes or rights.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding consultation for appointment of High Court judges:
I. The Chief Justice of a High Court is appointed after consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the State.
II. Other High Court judges are appointed after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the State and the Chief Justice of that High Court.
III. The Governor alone appoints the judges of a High Court.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. High Court judges are appointed by the President, following the prescribed consultation process; the Governor does not appoint them alone.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding qualification for appointment as a High Court judge is incorrect?
options: The person may have held judicial office in India for at least 10 years.
The person must be a citizen of India.
The person may qualify by being a distinguished jurist, even without satisfying the other requirements.
The person may have practised as an advocate of a High Court for at least 10 years.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is the distinguished-jurist qualification. Unlike the Supreme Court, the Constitution provides no such route for appointment as a High Court judge.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Article 219
(b) Article 217(1)(a)
(c) Article 217(1)(b) read with Article 124(4)
(d) Article 220

List-II
(i) Restriction on practice after retirement as a permanent judge
(ii) Oath or affirmation by High Court judges
(iii) Resignation addressed to the President
(iv) Removal on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Article 219—oath; Article 217(1)(a)—resignation; Article 217(1)(b) read with Article 124(4)—removal; Article 220—post-retirement practice restriction.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: A retired permanent High Court judge may plead or act before the Supreme Court.
Statement B: A retired permanent High Court judge may plead or act before any High Court, including the High Court where he or she served as a permanent judge.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
